124.m: "By the birth of whom in this world I might become the mother of a hero, / that [son] I would choose, O father of gods!" so she said, full of modesty.

124.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
upadekṣye vrataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dvādaśābdaphalapradam
tata āgatya te garbham ādhāsye yan manogatam
niṣpāpatāyāṃ jātāyāṃ sidhyanti hi manorathāḥ //
124.d:
कश्यप उवाच
उपदेक्ष्ये व्रतं श्रेष्ठं द्वादशाब्दफलप्रदम्
तत आगत्य ते गर्भम् आधास्ये यन् मनोगतम्
निष्पापतायां जातायां सिध्यन्ति हि मनोरथाः ॥
124.m: Kaśyapa said: / "I shall instruct you in an excellent observance that yields the fruit of twelve years; / then, having returned, I will place in you the embryo that is in your mind. / For when purity from sin has come about, desires do indeed succeed."

124.s:
brahmovāca
bhartṛvākyād ditiḥ prītā taṃ namasyāyatekṣaṇā
upadiṣṭaṃ vrataṃ cakre bhartrādiṣṭaṃ yathāvidhi //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भर्तृवाक्याद् दितिः प्रीता तं नमस्यायतेक्षणा
उपदिष्टं व्रतं चक्रे भर्त्रादिष्टं यथाविधि ॥
124.m: Brahmā said: / Pleased by her husband's word, Diti, the large-eyed woman, bowed to him / and performed as prescribed the observance that her husband had instructed and enjoined.

124.s:
tīrthasevāpātradānavratacaryādivarjitāḥ
katham āsādayiṣyanti prāṇino 'tra manorathān //
124.d:
तीर्थसेवापात्रदानव्रतचर्यादिवर्जिताः
कथम् आसादयिष्यन्ति प्राणिनो ऽत्र मनोरथान् ॥
124.m: Devoid of visiting tīrthas, gifts to worthy recipients, vows, and observances, / how shall living beings attain their desires in this world?

124.s:
tataś cīrṇe vrate tasyāṃ dityāṃ garbham adhārayat
punaḥ kāntām athovāca kaśyapas tāṃ ditiṃ rahaḥ //
124.d:
ततश् चीर्णे व्रते तस्यां दित्यां गर्भम् अधारयत्
पुनः कान्ताम् अथोवाच कश्यपस् तां दितिं रहः ॥
124.m: Then, when the observance had been performed, he established an embryo in that Diti. / Thereupon Kaśyapa spoke again in secret to his beloved Diti:

124.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
na prāpnuvanti yatkāmān munayo 'pi tapassthitāḥ
yathāvihitakarmāṅgaavajñayā tac chucismite //
124.d:
कश्यप उवाच
न प्राप्नुवन्ति यत्कामान् मुनयो ऽपि तपस्स्थिताः
यथाविहितकर्माङ्गअवज्ञया तच् छुचिस्मिते ॥
124.m: Kaśyapa said: / "O woman of bright smiles, that which even sages engaged in austerities do not attain their desires for, / is through disregarding the limbs of prescribed actions.

124.s:
ninditaṃ ca na kartavyaṃ saṃdhyayor ubhayor api
na svaptavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ muktakeśī ca no bhava //
124.d:
निन्दितं च न कर्तव्यं संध्ययोर् उभयोर् अपि
न स्वप्तव्यं न गन्तव्यं मुक्तकेशी च नो भव ॥
124.m: And what is blameworthy must not be done; at both twilights / one must not sleep, nor go about, and do not have your hair loose.

124.s:
bhoktavyaṃ subhage naiva kṣutaṃ vā jṛmbhaṇaṃ tathā
saṃdhyākāle na kartavyaṃ bhūtasaṃghasamākule //
124.d:
भोक्तव्यं सुभगे नैव क्षुतं वा जृम्भणं तथा
संध्याकाले न कर्तव्यं भूतसंघसमाकुले ॥
124.m: Food must not be eaten, O fortunate lady, nor sneezing or yawning / should be done at the twilight hour, which is filled with crowds of spirits.

124.s:
sāntardhānaṃ sadā kāryaṃ hasitaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ
gṛhāntadeśe saṃdhyāsu na sthātavyaṃ kadācana //
124.d:
सान्तर्धानं सदा कार्यं हसितं तु विशेषतः
गृहान्तदेशे संध्यासु न स्थातव्यं कदाचन ॥
124.m: Laughter, especially, should always be done with concealment; / one should never stay at the threshold of the house during twilights.

124.s:
muśalolūkhalādīni śūrpapīṭhapidhānakam
naivātikramaṇīyāni divā rātrau sadā priye //
124.d:
मुशलोलूखलादीनि शूर्पपीठपिधानकम्
नैवातिक्रमणीयानि दिवा रात्रौ सदा प्रिये ॥
124.m: Pestles, mortars, winnowing baskets, low seats, and lids / are never to be stepped over, by day or by night, always, my dear.

124.s:
udakśīrṣaṃ tu śayanaṃ na saṃdhyāsu viśeṣataḥ
vaktavyaṃ nānṛtaṃ kiṃcin nānyagehāṭanaṃ tathā //
124.d:
उदक्शीर्षं तु शयनं न संध्यासु विशेषतः
वक्तव्यं नानृतं किंचिन् नान्यगेहाटनं तथा ॥
124.m: Lying down with the head to the north, especially at twilight, [must be avoided]; / no untruth whatsoever should be spoken, nor wandering into other people's homes.

124.s:
kāntād anyo na vīkṣyas tu prayatnena naraḥ kvacit
ityādiniyamair yuktā yadi tvam anuvartase
tatas te bhavitā putras trailokyaiśvaryabhājanam //
124.d:
कान्ताद् अन्यो न वीक्ष्यस् तु प्रयत्नेन नरः क्वचित्
इत्यादिनियमैर् युक्ता यदि त्वम् अनुवर्तसे
ततस् ते भविता पुत्रस् त्रैलोक्यैश्वर्यभाजनम् ॥
124.m: With effort, no man other than your husband should ever be looked upon. / If, endowed with such observances, you conduct yourself [thus], / then your son will become a vessel of sovereignty over the three worlds."

124.s:
brahmovāca
tatheti pratijajñe sā bhartāraṃ lokapūjitam
gataś ca kaśyapo brahmann itaś cetaḥ surān prati //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेति प्रतिजज्ञे सा भर्तारं लोकपूजितम्
गतश् च कश्यपो ब्रह्मन्न् इतश् चेतः सुरान् प्रति ॥
124.m: Brahmā said: / "So be it," she promised her husband, who is honored by the worlds. / And Kaśyapa went, O Brahmin, hither and thither to the gods.

124.s:
diter garbho 'pi vavṛdhe balavān puṇyasaṃbhavaḥ
etat sarvaṃ mayo daityo māyayā vetti tattvataḥ //
124.d:
दितेर् गर्भो ऽपि ववृधे बलवान् पुण्यसंभवः
एतत् सर्वं मयो दैत्यो मायया वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥
124.m: Diti's embryo also grew, strong and born of merit. / Maya the Daitya knew all this accurately by his illusory power.

124.s:
indrasya sakhyam abhavan mayena prītipūrvakam
mayo gatvā rahaḥ prāha indraṃ sa vinayānvitaḥ //
124.d:
इन्द्रस्य सख्यम् अभवन् मयेन प्रीतिपूर्वकम्
मयो गत्वा रहः प्राह इन्द्रं स विनयान्वितः ॥
124.m: Indra had a friendship with Maya based on affection. / Going in secret, Maya, full of humility, said to Indra:

124.s:
diter danor abhiprāyaṃ vrataṃ garbhasya vardhanam
tasya vīryaṃ ca vividhaṃ prītyendrāya nyavedayat //
124.d:
दितेर् दनोर् अभिप्रायं व्रतं गर्भस्य वर्धनम्
तस्य वीर्यं च विविधं प्रीत्येन्द्राय न्यवेदयत् ॥
124.m: He lovingly reported to Indra the intention of Diti and Danu, / the observance, the growth of the embryo, and its manifold strength.

124.s:
viśvāsaikagṛhaṃ mitram apāyatrāsavarjitam
arjitaṃ sukṛtaṃ nānāvidhaṃ cet tad avāpyate //
124.d:
विश्वासैकगृहं मित्रम् अपायत्रासवर्जितम्
अर्जितं सुकृतं नानाविधं चेत् तद् अवाप्यते ॥
124.m: A friend who is the sole abode of trust, free from fear of danger— / if manifold merit has been accumulated, then such a friend is obtained.

124.s:
nārada uvāca
namuceś ca priyo bhrātā mayo daityo mahābalaḥ
bhrātṛhantrā kathaṃ maitryaṃ mayasyāsīt sureśvara //
124.d:
नारद उवाच
नमुचेश् च प्रियो भ्राता मयो दैत्यो महाबलः
भ्रातृहन्त्रा कथं मैत्र्यं मयस्यासीत् सुरेश्वर ॥
124.m: Nārada said: / The Daitya Maya, of great strength, was the dear brother of Namuci. / How did Maya have friendship with the slayer of his brother, O lord of gods?

124.s:
brahmovāca
daityānām adhipaś cāsīd balavān namuciḥ purā
indreṇa vairam abhavad bhīṣaṇaṃ lomaharṣaṇam //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दैत्यानाम् अधिपश् चासीद् बलवान् नमुचिः पुरा
इन्द्रेण वैरम् अभवद् भीषणं लोमहर्षणम् ॥
124.m: Brahmā said: / In the past, the mighty Namuci was the sovereign of the Daityas. / There arose a terrifying, hair-raising enmity with Indra.

124.s:
yuddhaṃ hitvā kadācid bho gacchantaṃ tu śatakratum
dṛṣṭvā daityapatiḥ śūro namuciḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt //
124.d:
युद्धं हित्वा कदाचिद् भो गच्छन्तं तु शतक्रतुम्
दृष्ट्वा दैत्यपतिः शूरो नमुचिः पृष्ठतो ऽन्वगात् ॥
124.m: Once, O sage, having abandoned the fight, Śatakratu was departing; / seeing him, the heroic lord of Daityas, Namuci, pursued him from behind.

124.s:
tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya śacībhartā bhayāturaḥ
airāvataṃ gajaṃ tyaktvā indraḥ phenam athāviśat //
124.d:
तम् आयान्तम् अभिप्रेक्ष्य शचीभर्ता भयातुरः
ऐरावतं गजं त्यक्त्वा इन्द्रः फेनम् अथाविशत् ॥
124.m: Seeing him approaching, Indra, the husband of Śacī, distressed by fear, / abandoned the elephant Airāvata and entered into foam.

124.s:
sa vajrapāṇis tarasā phenenaivāhanad ripum
namucir nāśam agamat tasya bhrātā mayo 'nujaḥ //
124.d:
स वज्रपाणिस् तरसा फेनेनैवाहनद् रिपुम्
नमुचिर् नाशम् अगमत् तस्य भ्राता मयो ऽनुजः ॥
124.m: He, the thunderbolt-handed, quickly struck the enemy with that very foam. / Namuci went to destruction; Maya was his younger brother.

124.s:
bhrātṛhantṛvināśāya tapas tepe mayo mahat
māyāṃ ca vividhām āpa devānām atibhīṣaṇām //
124.d:
भ्रातृहन्तृविनाशाय तपस् तेपे मयो महत्
मायां च विविधाम् आप देवानाम् अतिभीषणाम् ॥
124.m: To destroy the killer of his brother, Maya performed great austerities, / and obtained various illusory powers exceedingly terrifying to the gods.

124.s:
varāṃś cāvāpya tapasā viṣṇor lokaparāyaṇāt
dānaśauṇḍaḥ priyālāpī tadābhavad asau mayaḥ //
124.d:
वरांश् चावाप्य तपसा विष्णोर् लोकपरायणात्
दानशौण्डः प्रियालापी तदाभवद् असौ मयः ॥
124.m: Having obtained boons through austerities from Viṣṇu, who is devoted to the world, / that Maya then became proficient in giving and pleasant in speech.

124.s:
agnīṃś ca brāhmaṇān pūjya jetum indraṃ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ
dātāraṃ ca tadārthibhyaḥ stūyamānaṃ ca bandibhiḥ //
124.d:
अग्नींश् च ब्राह्मणान् पूज्य जेतुम् इन्द्रं कृतक्षणः
दातारं च तदार्थिभ्यः स्तूयमानं च बन्दिभिः ॥
124.m: Having honored the fires and Brahmins, resolved to conquer Indra, / giving to supplicants and being praised by bards,

124.s:
viditvā maghavā vāyor mayaṃ māyāvinaṃ ripum
upakrāntaṃ suyuddhāya vipro bhūtvā tam abhyagāt
śacībhartā mayaṃ daityaṃ provācedaṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
124.d:
विदित्वा मघवा वायोर् मयं मायाविनं रिपुम्
उपक्रान्तं सुयुद्धाय विप्रो भूत्वा तम् अभ्यगात्
शचीभर्ता मयं दैत्यं प्रोवाचेदं पुनः पुनः ॥
124.m: Maghavan, knowing through Vāyu that his enemy Maya, skilled in illusion, / had set out for a great battle, became a Brahmin and approached him. / The husband of Śacī said this repeatedly to the Daitya Maya:

124.s:
indra uvāca
dehi daityapate mahyam arthine 'pekṣitaṃ varam
tvāṃ śrutvā dātṛtilakam āgato 'haṃ dvijottamaḥ //
124.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
देहि दैत्यपते मह्यम् अर्थिने ऽपेक्षितं वरम्
त्वां श्रुत्वा दातृतिलकम् आगतो ऽहं द्विजोत्तमः ॥
124.m: Indra said: / "O lord of Daityas, grant the desired boon to me, a supplicant! / Having heard of you as the crest-jewel of givers, I, the best of the twice-born, have come."

124.s:
brahmovāca
mayo 'pi brāhmaṇaṃ matvā 'vadad dattaṃ mayā tava
vicārayanti kṛtino bahv alpaṃ vā puro 'rthini //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मयो ऽपि ब्राह्मणं मत्वा ऽवदद् दत्तं मया तव
विचारयन्ति कृतिनो बह्व् अल्पं वा पुरो ऽर्थिनि ॥
124.m: Brahmā said: / Maya also, thinking him to be a Brahmin, said: "It is granted by me to you." / Do the virtuous consider whether it is much or little before a supplicant?

124.s:
ity ukte tu hariḥ prāha sakhyam icche hy ahaṃ tvayā
indraṃ mayaḥ punaḥ prāha kim anena dvijottama //
124.d:
इत्य् उक्ते तु हरिः प्राह सख्यम् इच्छे ह्य् अहं त्वया
इन्द्रं मयः पुनः प्राह किम् अनेन द्विजोत्तम ॥
124.m: When this was spoken, Hari said: "I desire friendship with you." / Maya said again to Indra: "What is the use of this, O best of the twice-born?

124.s:
na tvayā mama vairaṃ bhoḥ svastīty āha harir mayam
tattvaṃ vadeti sa harir daityenoktaḥ svakaṃ vapuḥ //
124.d:
न त्वया मम वैरं भोः स्वस्तीत्य् आह हरिर् मयम्
तत्त्वं वदेति स हरिर् दैत्येनोक्तः स्वकं वपुः ॥
124.m: You have no enmity with me; hail!" So Hari said to Maya. / Addressed by the Daitya, "Speak the truth!" that Hari showed his own form / to the Daitya—

124.s:
darśayām āsa daityāya sahasrākṣaṃ yad ucyate
tataḥ savismayo daityo mayo harim uvāca ha //
124.d:
दर्शयाम् आस दैत्याय सहस्राक्षं यद् उच्यते
ततः सविस्मयो दैत्यो मयो हरिम् उवाच ह ॥
124.m: that which is called the thousand-eyed one. / Then the Daitya Maya, filled with astonishment, said to Hari:

124.s:
maya uvāca
kim idaṃ vajrapāṇis tvaṃ tavāyogyā kṛtiḥ sakhe //
124.d:
मय उवाच
किम् इदं वज्रपाणिस् त्वं तवायोग्या कृतिः सखे ॥
124.m: Maya said: / "What is this? You are the wielder of the thunderbolt! This deed is unworthy of you, my friend!"

124.s:
brahmovāca
pariṣvajya vihasyātha vṛttam ity abravīd dhariḥ
kenāpi sādhayanty atra paṇḍitāś ca samīhitam //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
परिष्वज्य विहस्याथ वृत्तम् इत्य् अब्रवीद् धरिः
केनापि साधयन्त्य् अत्र पण्डिताश् च समीहितम् ॥
124.m: Brahmā said: / Having embraced him and laughed, Hari said: "So it happened; / the wise accomplish what they desire by any means in this world."

124.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti śakrasya mayena mahatī hy abhūt
suprītir muniśārdūla mayo harihitaḥ sadā //
124.d:
ततः प्रभृति शक्रस्य मयेन महती ह्य् अभूत्
सुप्रीतिर् मुनिशार्दूल मयो हरिहितः सदा ॥
124.m: From that time forth, there was indeed great affection / between Śakra and Maya, O tiger among sages; Maya was ever devoted to Hari's welfare.

124.s:
indrasya bhavanaṃ gatvā tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayat
kiṃ me kṛtyam iti prāha mayaṃ māyāvinaṃ hariḥ //
124.d:
इन्द्रस्य भवनं गत्वा तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयत्
किं मे कृत्यम् इति प्राह मयं मायाविनं हरिः ॥
124.m: Having gone to Indra's abode, he reported everything to him. / Hari said to Maya, the master of illusion: "What should I do?"

124.s:
haraye ca mayo māyāṃ prādāt prītyā tathā hariḥ
prāptaḥ saṃprītimān āha kiṃ kṛtyaṃ maya tad vada //
124.d:
हरये च मयो मायां प्रादात् प्रीत्या तथा हरिः
प्राप्तः संप्रीतिमान् आह किं कृत्यं मय तद् वद ॥
124.m: And Maya affectionately gave illusory power to Hari; likewise Hari, / having received it and being delighted, said: "Tell me, Maya, what is to be done?"

124.s:
maya uvāca
agastyasyāśramaṃ gaccha tatrāste garbhiṇī ditiḥ
tasyāḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ kurvann āssva tatra kiyanti ca //
124.d:
मय उवाच
अगस्त्यस्याश्रमं गच्छ तत्रास्ते गर्भिणी दितिः
तस्याः शुश्रूषणं कुर्वन्न् आस्स्व तत्र कियन्ति च ॥
124.m: Maya said: / "Go to the hermitage of Agastya; pregnant Diti is staying there. / Rendering service to her, remain there for some

124.s:
ahāni maghavaṃs tasyā garbham āviśya vajradhṛk
vardhamānaṃ ca taṃ chindhi yāvad vaśyo 'thavā mṛtim
prāpnoti tāvad vajreṇa tato na bhavitā ripuḥ //
124.d:
अहानि मघवंस् तस्या गर्भम् आविश्य वज्रधृक्
वर्धमानं च तं छिन्धि यावद् वश्यो ऽथवा मृतिम्
प्राप्नोति तावद् वज्रेण ततो न भविता रिपुः ॥
124.m: days, O Maghavan, and having entered her womb, O bearer of the thunderbolt, / cut that growing [fetus] until it is subdued or meets death / with the thunderbolt; then there will be no enemy."

124.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā mayaṃ pūjya maghavān eka eva hi
vinītavat tadā prāyād ditiṃ mātaram añjasā
śuśrūṣamāṇas tāṃ devīṃ śakro daiteyamātaram
sā na jānāti tac cittaṃ śakrasya dviṣato ditiḥ
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा मयं पूज्य मघवान् एक एव हि
विनीतवत् तदा प्रायाद् दितिं मातरम् अञ्जसा
शुश्रूषमाणस् तां देवीं शक्रो दैतेयमातरम्
सा न जानाति तच् चित्तं शक्रस्य द्विषतो दितिः
124.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "So be it" and honoring Maya, Maghavan went alone, / like one who is humble, directly to mother Diti. / Śakra served that goddess, the mother of the Daiteyas; / she, Diti, did not know that intention of her enemy Śakra.

124.s:
garbhe sthitaṃ tu yad bhūtaṃ devendrasya viceṣṭitam
amoghaṃ tan munes tejaḥ kaśyapasya durāsadam //
124.d:
गर्भे स्थितं तु यद् भूतं देवेन्द्रस्य विचेष्टितम्
अमोघं तन् मुनेस् तेजः कश्यपस्य दुरासदम् ॥
124.m: The being that was in the womb, however, [aware of] the action of the lord of gods, / was the unfailing, invincible splendour of the sage Kaśyapa.

124.s:
tataḥ pragṛhya kuliśaṃ sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
antaḥpraveśakāmo 'sau bahukālaṃ samāvasan //
124.d:
ततः प्रगृह्य कुलिशं सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः
अन्तःप्रवेशकामो ऽसौ बहुकालं समावसन् ॥
124.m: Then, seizing the thunderbolt, Purandara, the thousand-eyed, / desiring to enter inside, resided there for a long time.

124.s:
saṃdhyodakśīrṣanidrāṃ tām avekṣya kuliśāyudhaḥ
idam antaram ity uktvā dityāḥ kukṣiṃ samāviśat //
124.d:
संध्योदक्शीर्षनिद्रां ताम् अवेक्ष्य कुलिशायुधः
इदम् अन्तरम् इत्य् उक्त्वा दित्याः कुक्षिं समाविशत् ॥
124.m: Seeing her asleep at twilight with her head to the north, the one whose weapon is the thunderbolt / said, "This is the opportunity!" and entered Diti's womb.

124.s:
antarvarti ca yad bhūtam indraṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtāyudham
hantukāmaṃ tadovāca punaḥ punar abhītavat //
124.d:
अन्तर्वर्ति च यद् भूतम् इन्द्रं दृष्ट्वा धृतायुधम्
हन्तुकामं तदोवाच पुनः पुनर् अभीतवत् ॥
124.m: And seeing Indra with raised weapon, desiring to kill it, / the being situated inside spoke repeatedly, as if fearless:

124.s:
garbhastha uvāca
kiṃ māṃ na rakṣase vajrin bhrātaraṃ tvaṃ jighāṃsasi
nāraṇe māraṇād anyat pātakaṃ vidyate mahat //
124.d:
गर्भस्थ उवाच
किं मां न रक्षसे वज्रिन् भ्रातरं त्वं जिघांससि
नारणे मारणाद् अन्यत् पातकं विद्यते महत् ॥
124.m:
The one in the womb said:
"Why do you not protect me, O wielder of the thunderbolt? Do you wish to slay your brother? / There is no other great sin greater than killing one who is not on a battlefield.

124.s:
ṛte yuddhān mahābāho śakra yudhyasva nirgate
mayi tasmān naitad evaṃ tava yuktaṃ bhaviṣyati //
124.d:
ऋते युद्धान् महाबाहो शक्र युध्यस्व निर्गते
मयि तस्मान् नैतद् एवं तव युक्तं भविष्यति ॥
124.m: Apart from battle, O mighty-armed Śakra, fight once I have emerged! / Therefore, this conduct of yours will not be right.

124.s:
śatakratuḥ sahasrākṣaḥ śacībhartā puraṃdaraḥ
vajrapāṇiḥ surendras tvaṃ te na yuktaṃ bhavet prabho //
124.d:
शतक्रतुः सहस्राक्षः शचीभर्ता पुरंदरः
वज्रपाणिः सुरेन्द्रस् त्वं ते न युक्तं भवेत् प्रभो ॥
124.m: You are Śatakratu, the thousand-eyed, the husband of Śacī, the destroyer of citadels, / with thunderbolt in hand, the lord of gods; this would not befit you, O lord!

124.s:
athavā yuddhakāmas tvaṃ mama niṣkramaṇaṃ yathā
tathā kuru mahābāho mārgād asmād apāsara //
124.d:
अथवा युद्धकामस् त्वं मम निष्क्रमणं यथा
तथा कुरु महाबाहो मार्गाद् अस्माद् अपासर ॥
124.m: Or, if you desire battle, arrange for my exit, / O mighty-armed one; step aside from this path!

124.s:
kumārge na pravartante mahānto 'pi vipadgatāḥ
avidyaś cāpy aśastraś ca naiva cāyudhasaṃgrahaḥ //
124.d:
कुमार्गे न प्रवर्तन्ते महान्तो ऽपि विपद्गताः
अविद्यश् चाप्य् अशस्त्रश् च नैव चायुधसंग्रहः ॥
124.m: Even when fallen into misfortune, great beings do not set out upon an evil path. / I have no knowledge, no weapon, nor any grasp of arms.

124.s:
tvaṃ vidyāvān vajrapāṇe māṃ nighnan kiṃ na lajjase
kurvanti garhitaṃ karma na kulīnāḥ kadācana //
124.d:
त्वं विद्यावान् वज्रपाणे मां निघ्नन् किं न लज्जसे
कुर्वन्ति गर्हितं कर्म न कुलीनाः कदाचन ॥
124.m: You possess knowledge, O wielder of the thunderbolt in hand; are you not ashamed to strike me? / Those born of noble family never perform a contemptible deed.

124.s:
hatvā vā kiṃ tu jāyeta yaśo vā puṇyam eva vā
vadhyante bhrātaraḥ kāmād garbhasthāḥ kiṃ nu pauruṣam //
124.d:
हत्वा वा किं तु जायेत यशो वा पुण्यम् एव वा
वध्यन्ते भ्रातरः कामाद् गर्भस्थाः किं नु पौरुषम् ॥
124.m: Or what fame, or what merit, would arise from killing? / If brothers residing in the womb are slain out of desire, what kind of manliness is that?

124.s:
yadi vā yuddhabhaktis te mayi bhrātar asaṃśayam
tato muṣṭiṃ puraskṛtya vajriṇe 'sau vyavasthitaḥ //
124.d:
यदि वा युद्धभक्तिस् ते मयि भ्रातर् असंशयम्
ततो मुष्टिं पुरस्कृत्य वज्रिणे ऽसौ व्यवस्थितः ॥
124.m: Or if you have a love for battle with me, brother, without doubt—" / Then, putting forth his fist, he stood ready against the wielder of the thunderbolt.

124.s:
bālaghātī brahmaghātī tathā viśvāsaghātakaḥ
evaṃbhūtaṃ phalaṃ śakra kasmān māṃ hantum udyataḥ //
124.d:
बालघाती ब्रह्मघाती तथा विश्वासघातकः
एवंभूतं फलं शक्र कस्मान् मां हन्तुम् उद्यतः ॥
124.m: "One who slays a child, one who slays a brahmin, and likewise a betrayer of trust— / such is the fruit, O Śakra! Why are you bent on killing me?

124.s:
yasyājñayā sarvam idaṃ vartate sacarācaram
sa hantā bālakaṃ māṃ vai kiṃ yaśaḥ kiṃ tu pauruṣam //
124.d:
यस्याज्ञया सर्वम् इदं वर्तते सचराचरम्
स हन्ता बालकं मां वै किं यशः किं तु पौरुषम् ॥
124.m: He by whose command all this moves, with all that is moving and unmoving— / if he slays me, an infant, what fame or what manliness is there?"

124.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ bruvantaṃ taṃ garbhaṃ ciccheda kuliśena saḥ
krodhāndhānāṃ lobhināṃ ca na ghṛṇā kvāpi vidyate //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं ब्रुवन्तं तं गर्भं चिच्छेद कुलिशेन सः
क्रोधान्धानां लोभिनां च न घृणा क्वापि विद्यते ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
As he spoke thus, he cut that fetus with the thunderbolt. / For those blinded by anger and filled with greed, no pity exists anywhere.

124.s:
na mamāra tato duḥkhād āhus te bhrātaro vayam
punaś ciccheda tān khaṇḍān mā vadhīr iti cābruvan //
124.d:
न ममार ततो दुःखाद् आहुस् ते भ्रातरो वयम्
पुनश् चिच्छेद तान् खण्डान् मा वधीर् इति चाब्रुवन् ॥
124.m: He did not die; then, out of distress, they said, "We are brothers!" / He cut those pieces again, and they said, "Do not kill!"

124.s:
viśvastān mātṛgarbhasthān nijabhrātṝñ śatakrato
dveṣavidhvastabuddhīnāṃ na citte karuṇākaṇaḥ //
124.d:
विश्वस्तान् मातृगर्भस्थान् निजभ्रातॄञ् शतक्रतो
द्वेषविध्वस्तबुद्धीनां न चित्ते करुणाकणः ॥
124.m: [He struck] his own brothers who trusted him, resting in their mother's womb, O Śatakratu! / In the minds of those whose intellect is ruined by hatred, there is not even a drop of compassion.

124.s:
evaṃ tu khaṇḍitaṃ khaṇḍaṃ hastapādādijīvavat
nirvikāraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā saptasapta suvismitaḥ //
124.d:
एवं तु खण्डितं खण्डं हस्तपादादिजीववत्
निर्विकारं ततो दृष्ट्वा सप्तसप्त सुविस्मितः ॥
124.m: Thus seeing each severed piece possessing life with hands, feet, and the like, / remaining unaltered in seven groups of seven, he was greatly astonished.

124.s:
ekavad bahurūpāṇi garbhasthāni śubhāni ca
rudanti bahurūpāṇi mā rutety abravīd dhariḥ //
124.d:
एकवद् बहुरूपाणि गर्भस्थानि शुभानि च
रुदन्ति बहुरूपाणि मा रुतेत्य् अब्रवीद् धरिः ॥
124.m: Remaining in the womb, beautiful and multiform like one, / the multiform beings wept, and Hari said, "Do not weep!"

124.s:
tatas te maruto jātā balavanto mahaujasaḥ
garbhasthā eva te 'nyonyam ūcuḥ śakraṃ gatabhramāḥ //
124.d:
ततस् ते मरुतो जाता बलवन्तो महौजसः
गर्भस्था एव ते ऽन्योन्यम् ऊचुः शक्रं गतभ्रमाः ॥
124.m: Then they became the Maruts, strong and possessed of great splendor. / While still in the womb, free from confusion, they said to one another and to Śakra:

124.s:
agastyaṃ muniśārdūlaṃ mātā yasyāśrame sthitā
asmatpitā tava bhrātā sakhyaṃ te bahu manyate //
124.d:
अगस्त्यं मुनिशार्दूलं माता यस्याश्रमे स्थिता
अस्मत्पिता तव भ्राता सख्यं ते बहु मन्यते ॥
124.m: "To Agastya, the tiger among sages, in whose hermitage our mother stays: / our father is your brother, and he values your friendship highly.

124.s:
asmān upari sasnehaṃ manas te vidmahe mune
na yat karoti śvapacaḥ pravṛttas tatra vajradhṛk //
124.d:
अस्मान् उपरि सस्नेहं मनस् ते विद्महे मुने
न यत् करोति श्वपचः प्रवृत्तस् तत्र वज्रधृक् ॥
124.m: We know your mind is affectionate toward us, O sage; / the bearer of the thunderbolt has undertaken what even an outcaste does not do!"

124.s:
ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā agastyo 'gāt sasaṃbhramaḥ
ditiṃ saṃbodhayām āsa vyathitāṃ garbhavedanāt //
124.d:
इत्य् एतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा अगस्त्यो ऽगात् ससंभ्रमः
दितिं संबोधयाम् आस व्यथितां गर्भवेदनात् ॥
124.m: Hearing this speech, Agastya came in haste, / and consoled Diti, who was afflicted by the pain in her womb.

124.s: tatrāgastyaḥ śacīkāntam aśapat kupito bhṛśam //
124.d: तत्रागस्त्यः शचीकान्तम् अशपत् कुपितो भृशम् ॥
124.m: There, Agastya, intensely enraged, cursed the beloved of Śacī.

124.s:
agastya uvāca
saṃgrāme ripavaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ paśyeyus te sadā hare
jīvatām eva maraṇam etad eva hi māninām
pṛṣṭhaṃ palāyamānānāṃ yat paśyanty ahitā raṇe //
124.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
संग्रामे रिपवः पृष्ठं पश्येयुस् ते सदा हरे
जीवताम् एव मरणम् एतद् एव हि मानिनाम्
पृष्ठं पलायमानानां यत् पश्यन्त्य् अहिता रणे ॥
124.m:
Agastya said:
"May your enemies always see your back in battle, O Hari! / For to proud men, this indeed is death while still living: / that enemies see the back of those fleeing in battle."

124.s:
brahmovāca
sāpi taṃ garbhasaṃsthaṃ ca śaśāpendraṃ ruṣā ditiḥ //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सापि तं गर्भसंस्थं च शशापेन्द्रं रुषा दितिः ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
Diti too, in anger, cursed Indra who was residing inside the womb.

124.s:
ditir uvāca
na pauruṣaṃ kṛtaṃ tasmāc chāpo 'yaṃ bhavitā tava
strībhiḥ paribhavaṃ prāpya rājyāt prabhraśyase hare //
124.d:
दितिर् उवाच
न पौरुषं कृतं तस्माच् छापो ऽयं भविता तव
स्त्रीभिः परिभवं प्राप्य राज्यात् प्रभ्रश्यसे हरे ॥
124.m:
Diti said:
"No manliness was shown, and therefore this curse shall fall upon you: / suffering defeat at the hands of women, you shall fall from your realm, O Hari!"

124.s:
brahmovāca
etasminn antare tatra kaśyapo vai prajāpatiḥ
prāyāc ca vyathito 'gastyāc chrutvā śakraviceṣṭitam
garbhāntaragataḥ śakraḥ pitaraṃ prāha bhītavat //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र कश्यपो वै प्रजापतिः
प्रायाच् च व्यथितो ऽगस्त्याच् छ्रुत्वा शक्रविचेष्टितम्
गर्भान्तरगतः शक्रः पितरं प्राह भीतवत् ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
In the meantime, the lord of creatures Kaśyapa arrived there, / distressed after hearing from Agastya of Śakra's conduct. / Śakra, stationed inside the womb, spoke fearfully to his father.

124.s:
śakra uvāca
agastyāc ca diteś caiva bibhemi kramituṃ bahiḥ //
124.d:
शक्र उवाच
अगस्त्याच् च दितेश् चैव बिभेमि क्रमितुं बहिः ॥
124.m:
Śakra said:
"I am afraid to step outside because of Agastya and Diti."

124.s:
brahmovāca
etasminn antare prāpya kaśyapo 'pi prajāpatiḥ
putrakarma ca tad dṛṣṭvā garbhāntaḥsthitim eva ca
ditiśāpam agastyasya śrutvāsau duḥkhito 'bhavat //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे प्राप्य कश्यपो ऽपि प्रजापतिः
पुत्रकर्म च तद् दृष्ट्वा गर्भान्तःस्थितिम् एव च
दितिशापम् अगस्त्यस्य श्रुत्वासौ दुःखितो ऽभवत् ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
In the meantime, having arrived, the lord of creatures Kaśyapa also, / seeing that deed of his son and his presence within the womb, / and hearing the curse of Diti and of Agastya, became sorrowful.

124.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
nirgaccha śakra putraitat pāpaṃ kiṃ kṛtavān asi
na nirmalakulotpannā manaḥ kurvanti pātake //
124.d:
कश्यप उवाच
निर्गच्छ शक्र पुत्रैतत् पापं किं कृतवान् असि
न निर्मलकुलोत्पन्ना मनः कुर्वन्ति पातके ॥
124.m:
Kaśyapa said:
"Come out, son Śakra! Why have you committed this sin? / Those born of a spotless family do not set their minds on sin."

124.s:
brahmovāca
sa nirgato vajrapāṇiḥ savrīḍo 'dhomukho 'bravīt
tanmūrtir eva vadati sadasacceṣṭitaṃ nṛṇām //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स निर्गतो वज्रपाणिः सव्रीडो ऽधोमुखो ऽब्रवीत्
तन्मूर्तिर् एव वदति सदसच्चेष्टितं नृणाम् ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
With thunderbolt in hand, he emerged; ashamed, with face cast down, he spoke. / A person's very bodily form reveals their good and bad deeds.

124.s:
śakra uvāca
yad uktam atra śreyaḥ syāt tatkartāham asaṃśayam //
124.d:
शक्र उवाच
यद् उक्तम् अत्र श्रेयः स्यात् तत्कर्ताहम् असंशयम् ॥
124.m:
Śakra said:
"Whatever is said to bring about welfare in this matter, that I shall surely do."

124.s:
brahmovāca
tato mamāntikaṃ prāyāl lokapālaiḥ sa kaśyapaḥ
sarvaṃ vṛttam athovāca punaḥ papraccha māṃ suraiḥ //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो ममान्तिकं प्रायाल् लोकपालैः स कश्यपः
सर्वं वृत्तम् अथोवाच पुनः पप्रच्छ मां सुरैः ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
Then that Kaśyapa approached my presence along with the guardians of the world. / He related the entire occurrence, and then questioned me alongside the gods,

124.s:
ditigarbhasya vai śāntiṃ sahasrākṣaviśāpatām
garbhasthānāṃ ca sarveṣām indreṇa saha mitratām //
124.d:
दितिगर्भस्य वै शान्तिं सहस्राक्षविशापताम्
गर्भस्थानां च सर्वेषाम् इन्द्रेण सह मित्रताम् ॥
124.m: about the pacification of Diti's womb, the release of the thousand-eyed one from the curse, / the friendship of all those in the womb with Indra,

124.s:
teṣām ārogyatāṃ cāpi śacībhartur adoṣatām
agastyadattaśāpasya viśāpatvam api kramāt //
124.d:
तेषाम् आरोग्यतां चापि शचीभर्तुर् अदोषताम्
अगस्त्यदत्तशापस्य विशापत्वम् अपि क्रमात् ॥
124.m: their state of health, the blamelessness of the husband of Śacī, / and gradually the liberation from the curse bestowed by Agastya.

124.s:
tato 'ham abravaṃ vākyaṃ kaśyapaṃ vinayānvitam
prajāpate kaśyapa tvaṃ vasubhir lokapālakaiḥ //
124.d:
ततो ऽहम् अब्रवं वाक्यं कश्यपं विनयान्वितम्
प्रजापते कश्यप त्वं वसुभिर् लोकपालकैः ॥
124.m: Then I spoke these words to Kaśyapa, who was full of humility: / 'O lord of creatures Kaśyapa, together with the Vasus and the guardians of the world,

124.s:
indreṇa sahitaḥ śīghraṃ gautamīṃ yāhi mānada
tatra snātvā maheśānaṃ stuhi sarvaiḥ samanvitaḥ //
124.d:
इन्द्रेण सहितः शीघ्रं गौतमीं याहि मानद
तत्र स्नात्वा महेशानं स्तुहि सर्वैः समन्वितः ॥
124.m: accompanied by Indra, go quickly to the Gautamī, O giver of honor! / Having bathed there, praise the great lord accompanied by all of them.

124.s:
tataḥ śivaprasādena sarvaṃ śreyo bhaved iti
tathety uktvā jagāmāsau kaśyapo gautamīṃ tadā //
124.d:
ततः शिवप्रसादेन सर्वं श्रेयो भवेद् इति
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा जगामासौ कश्यपो गौतमीं तदा ॥
124.m: Then, through the grace of Śiva, all welfare will come to pass.' / Saying 'So be it,' Kaśyapa then went to the Gautamī.

124.s:
snātvā tuṣṭāva deveśam ebhir eva padakramaiḥ
sarvaduḥkhāpanodāya dvayam eva prakīrtitam
gautamī vā puṇyanadī śivo vā karuṇākaraḥ //
124.d:
स्नात्वा तुष्टाव देवेशम् एभिर् एव पदक्रमैः
सर्वदुःखापनोदाय द्वयम् एव प्रकीर्तितम्
गौतमी वा पुण्यनदी शिवो वा करुणाकरः ॥
124.m: Having bathed, he praised the lord of gods with these very verses: / 'For removing all sorrow, only two are proclaimed: / either the sacred river Gautamī, or Śiva, the mine of compassion.'

124.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
pāhi śaṃkara deveśa pāhi lokanamaskṛta
pāhi pāvana vāgīśa pāhi pannagabhūṣaṇa //
124.d:
कश्यप उवाच
पाहि शंकर देवेश पाहि लोकनमस्कृत
पाहि पावन वागीश पाहि पन्नगभूषण ॥
124.m:
Kaśyapa said:
"Protect, O Śaṅkara, lord of gods! Protect, O you who are bowed to by the worlds! / Protect, O purifier, lord of speech! Protect, O serpent-adorned one!

124.s:
pāhi dharma vṛṣārūḍha pāhi vedatrayekṣaṇa
pāhi godhara lakṣmīśa pāhi śarva gajāmbara //
124.d:
पाहि धर्म वृषारूढ पाहि वेदत्रयेक्षण
पाहि गोधर लक्ष्मीश पाहि शर्व गजाम्बर ॥
124.m: Protect, O dharma, mounted upon the bull! Protect, O three-Veda-eyed one! / Protect, O bearer of the earth, lord of Lakṣmī! Protect, O Śarva, clothed in elephant hide!

124.s:
pāhi tripurahan nātha pāhi somārdhabhūṣaṇa
pāhi yajñeśa someśa pāhy abhīṣṭapradāyaka //
124.d:
पाहि त्रिपुरहन् नाथ पाहि सोमार्धभूषण
पाहि यज्ञेश सोमेश पाह्य् अभीष्टप्रदायक ॥
124.m: Protect, O destroyer of Tripura, O protector! Protect, O you adorned with the crescent moon! / Protect, O lord of sacrifice, lord of Soma! Protect, O bestower of desired boons!

124.s:
pāhi kāruṇyanilaya pāhi maṅgaladāyaka
pāhi prabhava sarvasya pāhi pālaka vāsava //
124.d:
पाहि कारुण्यनिलय पाहि मङ्गलदायक
पाहि प्रभव सर्वस्य पाहि पालक वासव ॥
124.m: Protect, O abode of compassion! Protect, O giver of auspiciousness! / Protect, O origin of all! Protect, O protector, O Vāsava!

124.s:
pāhi bhāskara vitteśa pāhi brahmanamaskṛta
pāhi viśveśa siddheśa pāhi pūrṇa namo 'stu te //
124.d:
पाहि भास्कर वित्तेश पाहि ब्रह्मनमस्कृत
पाहि विश्वेश सिद्धेश पाहि पूर्ण नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
124.m: Protect, O sun, O lord of wealth! Protect, O you bowed to by Brahmā! / Protect, O lord of the universe, lord of the perfected! Protect, O complete one! Homage be to you!

124.s:
ghorasaṃsārakāntārasaṃcārodvignacetasām
śarīriṇāṃ kṛpāsindho tvam eva śaraṇaṃ śiva //
124.d:
घोरसंसारकान्तारसंचारोद्विग्नचेतसाम्
शरीरिणां कृपासिन्धो त्वम् एव शरणं शिव ॥
124.m: For embodied beings whose minds are agitated by wandering in the dreadful wilderness of saṃsāra, / you alone are the refuge, O ocean of mercy, O Śiva!"

124.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ saṃstuvatas tasya purato 'bhūd vṛṣadhvajaḥ
vareṇa cchandayām āsa kaśyapaṃ taṃ prajāpatim //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं संस्तुवतस् तस्य पुरतो ऽभूद् वृषध्वजः
वरेण च्छन्दयाम् आस कश्यपं तं प्रजापतिम् ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
As he was praising him thus, the bull-bannered god appeared before him, / and invited Kaśyapa, that lord of creatures, with a boon.

124.s:
kaśyapo 'pi śivaṃ prāha vinītavad idaṃ vacaḥ
sa prāha vistareṇātha indrasya tu viceṣṭitam //
124.d:
कश्यपो ऽपि शिवं प्राह विनीतवद् इदं वचः
स प्राह विस्तरेणाथ इन्द्रस्य तु विचेष्टितम् ॥
124.m: Kaśyapa too spoke these words humbly to Śiva; / he then recounted in detail the deed of Indra,

124.s:
śāpaṃ nāśaṃ ca putrāṇāṃ parasparam amitratām
pāpaprāptiṃ tu śakrasya śāpaprāptiṃ tathaiva ca
tato vṛṣākapiḥ prāha ditiṃ cāgastyam eva ca //
124.d:
शापं नाशं च पुत्राणां परस्परम् अमित्रताम्
पापप्राप्तिं तु शक्रस्य शापप्राप्तिं तथैव च
ततो वृषाकपिः प्राह दितिं चागस्त्यम् एव च ॥
124.m: the curse, the destruction of his sons, their mutual enmity, / Śakra's incurring of sin, and likewise his incurring of the curse. / Then Vṛṣākapi spoke to Diti and to Agastya.

124.s:
śiva uvāca
maruto ye bhavatputrāḥ pañcāśac caikavarjitāḥ
sarve bhaveyuḥ subhagā bhaveyur yajñabhāginaḥ //
124.d:
शिव उवाच
मरुतो ये भवत्पुत्राः पञ्चाशच् चैकवर्जिताः
सर्वे भवेयुः सुभगा भवेयुर् यज्ञभागिनः ॥
124.m:
Śiva said:
Those Maruts who are your sons, forty-nine in number,
shall all be fortunate, and they shall be sharers in the sacrifice.

124.s: indreṇa sahitā nityaṃ vartayeyur mudānvitāḥ //
124.d: इन्द्रेण सहिता नित्यं वर्तयेयुर् मुदान्विताः ॥
124.m: Together with Indra, filled with joy, they shall always abide.

124.s:
indrasya tu havirbhāgo yatra yatra makhe bhavet
ādau tu marutas tatra bhaveyur nātra saṃśayaḥ //
124.d:
इन्द्रस्य तु हविर्भागो यत्र यत्र मखे भवेत्
आदौ तु मरुतस् तत्र भवेयुर् नात्र संशयः ॥
124.m:
Wherever there is an oblation portion for Indra in a sacrifice,
the Maruts shall indeed be there first; of this there is no doubt.

124.s:
marudbhiḥ sahitaṃ śakraṃ na jayeyuḥ kadācana
jetā bhavet sarvadaiva sukhaṃ tiṣṭha prajāpate //
124.d:
मरुद्भिः सहितं शक्रं न जयेयुः कदाचन
जेता भवेत् सर्वदैव सुखं तिष्ठ प्रजापते ॥
124.m:
No one shall ever conquer Śakra accompanied by the Maruts;
he shall always be the victor. Live in peace, O lord of creatures!

124.s:
adyaprabhṛti ye kuryur anayād bhrātṛghātanam
vaṃśacchedo vipattiś ca nityaṃ teṣāṃ bhaviṣyati //
124.d:
अद्यप्रभृति ये कुर्युर् अनयाद् भ्रातृघातनम्
वंशच्छेदो विपत्तिश् च नित्यं तेषां भविष्यति ॥
124.m:
From this day forth, whoever through injustice slays his brother,
there shall perpetually be ruin and the severance of their lineage.

124.s:
brahmovāca
agastyam ṛṣiśārdūlaṃ śaṃbhur apy āha yatnataḥ //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अगस्त्यम् ऋषिशार्दूलं शंभुर् अप्य् आह यत्नतः ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
Śambhu also earnestly spoke to Agastya, the tiger among ṛṣis:

124.s:
śaṃbhur uvāca
na kuryās tvaṃ ca kopaṃ ca śacībhartari vai mune
śamaṃ vraja mahāprājña marutas tv amarā bhavan //
124.d:
शंभुर् उवाच
न कुर्यास् त्वं च कोपं च शचीभर्तरि वै मुने
शमं व्रज महाप्राज्ञ मरुतस् त्व् अमरा भवन् ॥

124.s:
brahmovāca
ditiṃ cāpi śivaḥ prāha prasanno vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दितिं चापि शिवः प्राह प्रसन्नो वृषभध्वजः ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
Graciously pleased, Śiva whose banner is the bull spoke also to Diti:

124.s:
śiva uvāca
eko bhūyān mama sutas trailokyaiśvaryamaṇḍitaḥ
ity evaṃ cintayantī tvaṃ tapase niyatābhavaḥ //
124.d:
शिव उवाच
एको भूयान् मम सुतस् त्रैलोक्यैश्वर्यमण्डितः
इत्य् एवं चिन्तयन्ती त्वं तपसे नियताभवः ॥
124.m:
Śiva said:
"'May I have one great son adorned with sovereignty over the three worlds'—
thinking thus, you remained restrained in penance.

124.s:
tad etat saphalaṃ te 'dya putrā bahuguṇāḥ śubhāḥ
abhavan balinaḥ śūrās tasmāj jahi manorujam
anyān api varān subhrūr yācasva gatasaṃbhramā //
124.d:
तद् एतत् सफलं ते ऽद्य पुत्रा बहुगुणाः शुभाः
अभवन् बलिनः शूरास् तस्माज् जहि मनोरुजम्
अन्यान् अपि वरान् सुभ्रूर् याचस्व गतसंभ्रमा ॥
124.m:
Today that has borne fruit: your sons, endowed with many good qualities, auspicious,
powerful, and heroic, have come into being; therefore abandon your heartache.
O woman of lovely brows, freed from anxiety, ask for other boons as well!"

124.s:
brahmovāca
tad etad vacanaṃ śrutvā devadevasya sā ditiḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭā natvā śaṃbhuṃ vākyam athābravīt //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् एतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा देवदेवस्य सा दितिः
कृताञ्जलिपुटा नत्वा शंभुं वाक्यम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing these words of the god of gods, that Diti,
with folded hands and having bowed, then spoke these words to Śambhu:

124.s:
ditir uvāca
loke yad etat paramaṃ yat pitroḥ putradarśanam
viśeṣeṇa tu tan mātuḥ priyaṃ syāt surapūjita //
124.d:
दितिर् उवाच
लोके यद् एतत् परमं यत् पित्रोः पुत्रदर्शनम्
विशेषेण तु तन् मातुः प्रियं स्यात् सुरपूजित ॥
124.m:
Diti said:
"In this world, that supreme sight of a son by his parents,
O one worshiped by the gods, is especially dear to a mother.

124.s:
tatrāpi rūpasaṃpattiśauryavikramavān bhavet
eko 'pi tanayaḥ kiṃtu bahavaś cet kim ucyate //
124.d:
तत्रापि रूपसंपत्तिशौर्यविक्रमवान् भवेत्
एको ऽपि तनयः किंतु बहवश् चेत् किम् उच्यते ॥
124.m:
Even then, if there should be even one son endowed with beauty, valor, and prowess,
what need be said if there are many?

124.s:
matputrās te prabhāvāc ca jetāro balino dhruvam
indrasya bhrātaraḥ satyaṃ putrāś caiva prajāpateḥ //
124.d:
मत्पुत्रास् ते प्रभावाच् च जेतारो बलिनो ध्रुवम्
इन्द्रस्य भ्रातरः सत्यं पुत्राश् चैव प्रजापतेः ॥
124.m:
By your power my sons are certainly victorious and strong,
the true brothers of Indra and indeed the sons of the lord of creatures,

124.s:
agastyasya prasādāc ca gaṅgāyāś ca prasādataḥ
yatra deva prasādas te tac chubhaṃ ko 'tra saṃśayaḥ //
124.d:
अगस्त्यस्य प्रसादाच् च गङ्गायाश् च प्रसादतः
यत्र देव प्रसादस् ते तच् छुभं को ऽत्र संशयः ॥
124.m:
and by the grace of Agastya, and by the grace of Gaṅgā.
Where your grace is present, O god, that is auspicious; what doubt is there here?

124.s:
kṛtārthāhaṃ tathāpi tvāṃ bhaktyā vijñāpayāmy aham
śṛṇuṣva deva vacanaṃ kuruṣva ca jagaddhitam //
124.d:
कृतार्थाहं तथापि त्वां भक्त्या विज्ञापयाम्य् अहम्
शृणुष्व देव वचनं कुरुष्व च जगद्धितम् ॥
124.m:
I am fulfilled; nonetheless, with devotion I make a request of you.
Listen, O god, to my word, and bring about the welfare of the world!"

124.s:
brahmovāca
vadety uktā jagaddhātrā ditir namrābravīd idam //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वदेत्य् उक्ता जगद्धात्रा दितिर् नम्राब्रवीद् इदम् ॥
124.m:
Brahmā said:
Being told, "Speak," by the upholder of the world, Diti humbly spoke this:

124.s:
ditir uvāca
saṃtatiprāpaṇaṃ loke durlabhaṃ suravandita
viśeṣeṇa priyaṃ mātuḥ putraś cet kiṃ nu varṇyate //
124.d:
दितिर् उवाच
संततिप्रापणं लोके दुर्लभं सुरवन्दित
विशेषेण प्रियं मातुः पुत्रश् चेत् किं नु वर्ण्यते ॥
124.m:
Diti said:
"Obtaining offspring is hard to attain in the world, O one praised by the gods,
and a son is especially dear to a mother; what more can be described?

124.s:
sa cāpi guṇavāñ śrīmān āyuṣmān yadi jāyate
kiṃ tu svargeṇa deveśa pārameṣṭhyapadena vā //
124.d:
स चापि गुणवाञ् श्रीमान् आयुष्मान् यदि जायते
किं तु स्वर्गेण देवेश पारमेष्ठ्यपदेन वा ॥
124.m:
And if he is born virtuous, prosperous, and long-lived,
what need is there, O lord of gods, of heaven or the state of Parameṣṭhin?

124.s:
sarveṣām api bhūtānām ihāmutra phalaiṣiṇām
guṇavatputrasaṃprāptir abhīṣṭā sarvadaiva ca
tasmād āplavanād atra kriyatāṃ samanugrahaḥ //
124.d:
सर्वेषाम् अपि भूतानाम् इहामुत्र फलैषिणाम्
गुणवत्पुत्रसंप्राप्तिर् अभीष्टा सर्वदैव च
तस्माद् आप्लवनाद् अत्र क्रियतां समनुग्रहः ॥

124.s:
śaṃkara uvāca
mahāpāpaphalaṃ cedaṃ yad etad anapatyatā
striyā vā puruṣasyāpi vandhyatvaṃ yadi jāyate //
124.d:
शंकर उवाच
महापापफलं चेदं यद् एतद् अनपत्यता
स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्यापि वन्ध्यत्वं यदि जायते ॥
124.m:
Śaṅkara said:
"This childlessness is the result of a great sin,
if barrenness occurs in a woman or even in a man.

124.s:
tad atra snānamātreṇa taddoṣo nāśam āpnuyāt
snātvā tatra phalaṃ dadyāt stotram etac ca yaḥ paṭhet //
124.d:
तद् अत्र स्नानमात्रेण तद्दोषो नाशम् आप्नुयात्
स्नात्वा तत्र फलं दद्यात् स्तोत्रम् एतच् च यः पठेत् ॥
124.m:
By mere bathing here, that flaw will meet with destruction.
Whoever, having bathed there, gives fruit and recites this hymn,

124.s:
sa tu putram avāpnoti trimāsasnānadānataḥ
aputriṇī tv atra snānaṃ kṛtvā putram avāpnuyāt //
124.d:
स तु पुत्रम् अवाप्नोति त्रिमासस्नानदानतः
अपुत्रिणी त्व् अत्र स्नानं कृत्वा पुत्रम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
124.m:
attains a son through bathing and giving for three months.
A childless woman, having bathed here, will obtain a son.

124.s:
ṛtusnātā tu yā kācit tatra snātā sutāṃl labhet
trimāsābhyantaraṃ yā tu gurviṇī bhaktitas tv iha //
124.d:
ऋतुस्नाता तु या काचित् तत्र स्नाता सुतांल् लभेत्
त्रिमासाभ्यन्तरं या तु गुर्विणी भक्तितस् त्व् इह ॥
124.m:
Any woman who has bathed after her season and bathes there will obtain sons.
A pregnant woman who, within three months, with devotion here,

124.s:
phalaiḥ snātvā tu māṃ paśyet stotreṇa stauti māṃ tathā
tasyāḥ śakrasamaḥ putro jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
124.d:
फलैः स्नात्वा तु मां पश्येत् स्तोत्रेण स्तौति मां तथा
तस्याः शक्रसमः पुत्रो जायते नात्र संशयः ॥
124.m:
having bathed with fruits, beholds me and likewise praises me with the hymn,
to her is born a son equal to Śakra; of this there is no doubt.

124.s:
pitṛdoṣaiś ca ye putraṃ na labhante dite śṛṇu
dhanāpahāradoṣaiś ca tatraiṣā niṣkṛtiḥ parā //
124.d:
पितृदोषैश् च ये पुत्रं न लभन्ते दिते शृणु
धनापहारदोषैश् च तत्रैषा निष्कृतिः परा ॥
124.m:
And those who do not obtain a son due to the sins of their ancestors, hear, O Diti,
or due to sins of stealing wealth—for that, this is the supreme expiation:

124.s:
tatraiṣāṃ piṇḍadānena pitṝṇāṃ prīṇanena ca
kiṃcit suvarṇadānena tataḥ putro bhaved dhruvam //
124.d:
तत्रैषां पिण्डदानेन पितॄणां प्रीणनेन च
किंचित् सुवर्णदानेन ततः पुत्रो भवेद् ध्रुवम् ॥
124.m:
By offering rice-balls to them there, and by propitiating the ancestors,
and by the gift of some gold, a son will certainly be born to them.

124.s:
ye nyāsādyapahartāro ratnāpahnavakārakāḥ
śrāddhakarmavihīnāś ca teṣāṃ vaṃśo na vardhate //
124.d:
ये न्यासाद्यपहर्तारो रत्नापह्नवकारकाः
श्राद्धकर्मविहीनाश् च तेषां वंशो न वर्धते ॥
124.m:
Those who steal deposits and the like, those who conceal jewels,
and those devoid of ancestral rites—their lineage does not increase.

124.s:
doṣiṇāṃ tu paretānāṃ gatir eṣā bhaved iti
saṃtatir jāyatāṃ ślāghyā jīvatāṃ tīrthasevanāt //
124.d:
दोषिणां तु परेतानां गतिर् एषा भवेद् इति
संततिर् जायतां श्लाघ्या जीवतां तीर्थसेवनात् ॥
124.m:
Such is the fate of the deceased who are sinful;
may praiseworthy offspring be born to the living through resorting to this holy place.

124.s:
saṃgame ditigaṅgāyāḥ snātvā siddheśvaraṃ prabhum
anādyapāram ajaraṃ citsadānandavigraham //
124.d:
संगमे दितिगङ्गायाः स्नात्वा सिद्धेश्वरं प्रभुम्
अनाद्यपारम् अजरं चित्सदानन्दविग्रहम् ॥
124.m:
Having bathed at the confluence of Diti and the Gaṅgā, before the lord Siddheśvara,
who is without beginning or end, unaging, whose form is consciousness and eternal bliss,

124.s:
devarṣisiddhagandharvayogīśvaraniṣevitam
liṅgātmakaṃ mahādevaṃ jyotirmayam anāmayam //
124.d:
देवर्षिसिद्धगन्धर्वयोगीश्वरनिषेवितम्
लिङ्गात्मकं महादेवं ज्योतिर्मयम् अनामयम् ॥
124.m:
resorted to by divine seers, siddhas, gandharvas, and lords of yogins,
the great god in the form of a liṅga, full of light and free from ailment,

124.s:
pūjayitvopacāraiś ca nityaṃ bhaktyā yatavrataḥ
stotreṇānena yaḥ stauti caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca //
124.d:
पूजयित्वोपचारैश् च नित्यं भक्त्या यतव्रतः
स्तोत्रेणानेन यः स्तौति चतुर्दश्यष्टमीषु च ॥
124.m:
having worshiped him with offerings constantly, with devotion and restrained in vows,
whoever praises him with this hymn on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days,

124.s:
yathāśaktyā svarṇadānaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojanam
yaḥ karoty atra gaṅgāyāṃ sa putraśatam āpnuyāt //
124.d:
यथाशक्त्या स्वर्णदानं ब्राह्मणानां च भोजनम्
यः करोत्य् अत्र गङ्गायां स पुत्रशतम् आप्नुयात् ॥
124.m:
and according to his ability makes a gift of gold and the feeding of brāhmaṇas
here at the Gaṅgā, he shall obtain a hundred sons.

124.s:
saṃprāpya sakalān kāmān ante śivapuraṃ vrajet
stotreṇānena yaḥ kaścid yatra kvāpi stavīti mām
ṣaṇmāsāt putram āpnoti api vandhyāpy aśaṅkitam //
124.d:
संप्राप्य सकलान् कामान् अन्ते शिवपुरं व्रजेत्
स्तोत्रेणानेन यः कश्चिद् यत्र क्वापि स्तवीति माम्
षण्मासात् पुत्रम् आप्नोति अपि वन्ध्याप्य् अशङ्कितम् ॥
124.m:
Having attained all desires, in the end he goes to the city of Śiva.
Whoever praises me with this hymn anywhere whatsoever,
within six months obtains a son, even a barren woman, without doubt."

124.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ putratīrtham udāhṛtam
tatra tu snānadānādyaiḥ sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt //
124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पुत्रतीर्थम् उदाहृतम्
तत्र तु स्नानदानाद्यैः सर्वकामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥

124.s:
marudbhiḥ saha maitryeṇa mitratīrthaṃ tad ucyate
niṣpāpatvena cendrasya śakratīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
124.d:
मरुद्भिः सह मैत्र्येण मित्रतीर्थं तद् उच्यते
निष्पापत्वेन चेन्द्रस्य शक्रतीर्थं तद् उच्यते ॥
124.m:
Because of friendship with the Maruts, it is called Mitratīrtha;
and because of Indra's sinlessness, it is called Śakratīrtha.

124.s:
aindrīṃ śriyaṃ yatra lebhe tat tīrthaṃ kamalābhidham
etāni sarvatīrthāni sarvābhīṣṭapradāni hi //
124.d:
ऐन्द्रीं श्रियं यत्र लेभे तत् तीर्थं कमलाभिधम्
एतानि सर्वतीर्थानि सर्वाभीष्टप्रदानि हि ॥
124.m:
Where he obtained the prosperity of Indra, that holy place is named Kamalā.
All these holy places indeed grant all desired things.

124.s:
sarvaṃ bhaviṣyatīty uktvā śivaś cāntaradhīyata
kṛtakṛtyāś ca te jagmuḥ sarva eva yathāgatam
tīrthānāṃ puṇyadaṃ tatra lakṣam ekaṃ prakīrtitam //
124.d:
सर्वं भविष्यतीत्य् उक्त्वा शिवश् चान्तरधीयत
कृतकृत्याश् च ते जग्मुः सर्व एव यथागतम्
तीर्थानां पुण्यदं तत्र लक्षम् एकं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
124.m:
Saying, "All shall be so," Śiva vanished.
And having achieved their purpose, they all departed just as they had come.
One hundred thousand merit-giving holy places are celebrated there.

125.s:
brahmovāca
yamatīrtham iti khyātaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītivardhanam
dṛṣṭādṛṣṭeṣṭadaṃ sarvadevarṣigaṇasevitam //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यमतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं पितॄणां प्रीतिवर्धनम्
दृष्टादृष्टेष्टदं सर्वदेवर्षिगणसेवितम् ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
There is the one renowned as Yamatīrtha, which increases the pleasure of the ancestors,
giving desired things seen and unseen, resorted to by all the hosts of gods and ṛṣis.

125.s:
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
anuhrāda iti khyātaḥ kapoto balavān abhūt //
125.d:
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्
अनुह्राद इति ख्यातः कपोतो बलवान् अभूत् ॥
125.m:
I will tell of its power, which completely destroys all sins.
There was a powerful pigeon known as Anuhrāda.

125.s:
tasya bhāryā hetināmnī pakṣiṇī kāmarūpiṇī
mṛtyoḥ pautro hy anuhrādo dauhitrī hetir eva ca //
125.d:
तस्य भार्या हेतिनाम्नी पक्षिणी कामरूपिणी
मृत्योः पौत्रो ह्य् अनुह्रादो दौहित्री हेतिर् एव च ॥
125.m:
His wife was a bird named Hetī, able to change her form at will.
Anuhrāda was the grandson of Mṛtyu, and Hetī was the daughter's daughter.

125.s:
kālenātha tayoḥ putrāḥ pautrāś caiva babhūvire
tasya śatruś ca balavān ulūko nāma pakṣirāṭ //
125.d:
कालेनाथ तयोः पुत्राः पौत्राश् चैव बभूविरे
तस्य शत्रुश् च बलवान् उलूको नाम पक्षिराट् ॥
125.m:
In the course of time, sons and grandsons were born to the two of them.
He had a powerful enemy, a king of birds named Ulūka.

125.s:
tasya putrāś ca pautrāś ca āgneyās te balotkaṭāḥ
tayoś ca vairam abhavad bahukālaṃ dvijanmanoḥ //
125.d:
तस्य पुत्राश् च पौत्राश् च आग्नेयास् ते बलोत्कटाः
तयोश् च वैरम् अभवद् बहुकालं द्विजन्मनोः ॥
125.m:
His sons and grandsons were fiery and fierce in strength;
and between those two birds there was enmity for a long time.

125.s:
gaṅgāyā uttare tīre kapotasyāśramo 'bhavat
tasyāś ca dakṣiṇe kūla ulūko nāma pakṣirāṭ //
125.d:
गङ्गाया उत्तरे तीरे कपोतस्याश्रमो ऽभवत्
तस्याश् च दक्षिणे कूल उलूको नाम पक्षिराट् ॥
125.m:
On the northern bank of the Gaṅgā was the hermitage of the pigeon,
and on its southern bank the king of birds named Ulūka

125.s:
vāsaṃ cakre tatra putraiḥ pautraiś ca dvijasattama
tayoś ca yuddham abhavad bahukālaṃ viruddhayoḥ //
125.d:
वासं चक्रे तत्र पुत्रैः पौत्रैश् च द्विजसत्तम
तयोश् च युद्धम् अभवद् बहुकालं विरुद्धयोः ॥
125.m:
made his dwelling with his sons and grandsons, O best of the twice-born;
and a war took place between the two enemies for a long time.

125.s:
putraiḥ pautraiś ca vṛtayor balinor balibhiḥ saha
ulūko vā kapoto vā naivāpnoti jayājayau //
125.d:
पुत्रैः पौत्रैश् च वृतयोर् बलिनोर् बलिभिः सह
उलूको वा कपोतो वा नैवाप्नोति जयाजयौ ॥
125.m:
Surrounded by sons and grandsons, the two mighty ones with their mighty followers,
neither the owl nor the pigeon attained victory or defeat.

125.s:
kapoto yamam ārādhya mṛtyuṃ paitāmahaṃ tathā
yāmyam astram avāpyātha sarvebhyo 'py adhiko 'bhavat //
125.d:
कपोतो यमम् आराध्य मृत्युं पैतामहं तथा
याम्यम् अस्त्रम् अवाप्याथ सर्वेभ्यो ऽप्य् अधिको ऽभवत् ॥
125.m:
Worshipping Yama and death derived from Pitāmaha,
and obtaining the weapon of Yama, the dove became superior to all.

125.s:
tatholūko 'gnim ārādhya balavān abhavad bhṛśam
varair unmattayor yuddham abhavac cātibhīṣaṇam //
125.d:
तथोलूको ऽग्निम् आराध्य बलवान् अभवद् भृशम्
वरैर् उन्मत्तयोर् युद्धम् अभवच् चातिभीषणम् ॥
125.m:
Likewise, the owl, having worshipped Agni, became exceedingly strong.
Between the two, intoxicated by boons, an extremely terrifying battle took place.

125.s:
tatrāgneyam ulūko 'pi kapotāyāstram ākṣipat
kapoto 'py atha pāśān vai yāmyān ākṣipya śatrave //
125.d:
तत्राग्नेयम् उलूको ऽपि कपोतायास्त्रम् आक्षिपत्
कपोतो ऽप्य् अथ पाशान् वै याम्यान् आक्षिप्य शत्रवे ॥
125.m:
There the owl hurled the weapon of Agni at the dove;
and the dove hurled the nooses of Yama at the enemy.

125.s:
ulūkāyātha daṇḍaṃ ca mṛtyupāśān avāsṛjat
punas tad abhavad yuddhaṃ purāḍibakayor yathā //
125.d:
उलूकायाथ दण्डं च मृत्युपाशान् अवासृजत्
पुनस् तद् अभवद् युद्धं पुराडिबकयोर् यथा ॥
125.m:
Then [the dove] discharged the staff and the nooses of death at the owl.
Once again that battle was like that of the āḍi bird and the crane in ancient times.

125.s:
hetiḥ kapotakī dṛṣṭvā jvalanaṃ prāptam antike
pativratā mahāyuddhe bhartuḥ sā duḥkhavihvalā //
125.d:
हेतिः कपोतकी दृष्ट्वा ज्वलनं प्राप्तम् अन्तिके
पतिव्रता महायुद्धे भर्तुः सा दुःखविह्वला ॥
125.m:
Seeing the fire arrive near, the female dove Heti,
a devoted wife, was overwhelmed with grief for her husband in that great battle.

125.s:
agninā veṣṭyamānāṃś ca putrān dṛṣṭvā viśeṣataḥ
sā gatvā jvalanaṃ hetis tuṣṭāva vividhoktibhiḥ //
125.d:
अग्निना वेष्ट्यमानांश् च पुत्रान् दृष्ट्वा विशेषतः
सा गत्वा ज्वलनं हेतिस् तुष्टाव विविधोक्तिभिः ॥
125.m:
And seeing her sons especially enveloped by fire,
that Heti went to the fire and praised [him] with various words.

125.s:
hetir uvāca
rūpaṃ na dānaṃ na parokṣam asti
yasyātmabhūtaṃ ca padārthajātam
aśnanti havyāni ca yena devāḥ
svāhāpatiṃ yajñabhujaṃ namasye
125.d:
हेतिर् उवाच
रूपं न दानं न परोक्षम् अस्ति
यस्यात्मभूतं च पदार्थजातम्
अश्नन्ति हव्यानि च येन देवाः
स्वाहापतिं यज्ञभुजं नमस्ये
125.m:
Heti said:
[To him] whose form is neither an offering nor invisible,
who is the essential nature of the host of existing things,
and by means of whom the gods eat the oblations—
I bow to the lord of Svāhā, the consumer of sacrifice,

125.s:
mukhabhūtaṃ ca devānāṃ devānāṃ havyavāhanam
hotāraṃ cāpi devānāṃ devānāṃ dūtam eva ca //
125.d:
मुखभूतं च देवानां देवानां हव्यवाहनम्
होतारं चापि देवानां देवानां दूतम् एव च ॥
125.m:
who is the mouth of the gods, the bearer of oblations for the gods,
the invoker-priest of the gods, and the messenger of the gods.

125.s:
taṃ devaṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmi ādidevaṃ vibhāvasum
antaḥ sthitaḥ prāṇarūpo bahiś cānnaprado hi yaḥ
yo yajñasādhanaṃ yāmi śaraṇaṃ taṃ dhanaṃjayam //
125.d:
तं देवं शरणं यामि आदिदेवं विभावसुम्
अन्तः स्थितः प्राणरूपो बहिश् चान्नप्रदो हि यः
यो यज्ञसाधनं यामि शरणं तं धनंजयम् ॥
125.m:
I go for refuge to that god, the primordial god, the radiant one,
who dwells within in the form of breath and outside provides food,
who is the instrument of sacrifice—I go for refuge to that Dhanaṃjaya.

125.s:
agnir uvāca
amogham etad astraṃ me nyastaṃ yuddhe kapotaki
yatra viśramayed astraṃ tan me brūhi pativrate //
125.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अमोघम् एतद् अस्त्रं मे न्यस्तं युद्धे कपोतकि
यत्र विश्रमयेद् अस्त्रं तन् मे ब्रूहि पतिव्रते ॥
125.m:
Agni said:
This weapon of mine, cast in battle, is unfailing, female dove.
Tell me, devoted wife, where the weapon may come to rest.

125.s:
kapoty uvāca
mayi viśramyatām astraṃ na putre na ca bhartari
satyavāg bhava havyeśa jātavedo namo 'stu te //
125.d:
कपोत्य् उवाच
मयि विश्रम्यताम् अस्त्रं न पुत्रे न च भर्तरि
सत्यवाग् भव हव्येश जातवेदो नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
125.m:
The female dove said:
Let the weapon come to rest on me, not on my son and not on my husband.
Be true to your word, lord of oblations, Jātavedas! Homage to you!

125.s:
jātavedā uvāca
tuṣṭo 'smi tava vākyena bhartṛbhaktyā pativrate
tavāpi bhartṛputrāṇāṃ heti kṣemaṃ dadāmy aham //
125.d:
जातवेदा उवाच
तुष्टो ऽस्मि तव वाक्येन भर्तृभक्त्या पतिव्रते
तवापि भर्तृपुत्राणां हेति क्षेमं ददाम्य् अहम् ॥
125.m:
Jātavedas said:
I am pleased by your word and your devotion to your husband, devoted wife.
O Heti, I grant safety to you and to your husband and sons.

125.s:
āgneyam etad astraṃ me na bhartāraṃ sutān api
na tvāṃ dahet tato yāhi sukhena tvaṃ kapotaki //
125.d:
आग्नेयम् एतद् अस्त्रं मे न भर्तारं सुतान् अपि
न त्वां दहेत् ततो याहि सुखेन त्वं कपोतकि ॥
125.m:
This fiery weapon of mine shall not burn your husband nor your sons,
nor shall it burn you; therefore go happily, female dove!

125.s:
brahmovāca
etasminn antare tatra ulūkī dadṛśe patim
veṣṭyamānaṃ yāmyapāśair yamadaṇḍena tāḍitam
ulūkī duḥkhitā bhūtvā yamaṃ prāyād bhayāturā //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र उलूकी ददृशे पतिम्
वेष्ट्यमानं याम्यपाशैर् यमदण्डेन ताडितम्
उलूकी दुःखिता भूत्वा यमं प्रायाद् भयातुरा ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
In the meantime, the female owl saw her husband
enveloped by the nooses of Yama, struck by Yama's staff.
Becoming sorrowful and afflicted with fear, the female owl approached Yama.

125.s:
ulūky uvāca
tvadbhītā anudravante janās
tvadbhītā brahmacaryaṃ caranti
tvadbhītāḥ sādhu caranti dhīrās
tvadbhītāḥ karmaniṣṭhā bhavanti
125.d:
उलूक्य् उवाच
त्वद्भीता अनुद्रवन्ते जनास्
त्वद्भीता ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति
त्वद्भीताः साधु चरन्ति धीरास्
त्वद्भीताः कर्मनिष्ठा भवन्ति

125.s:
tvadbhītā anāśakam ācaranti
grāmād araṇyam abhi yac caranti
tvadbhītāḥ saumyatām āśrayante
tvadbhītāḥ somapānaṃ bhajante
125.d:
त्वद्भीता अनाशकम् आचरन्ति
ग्रामाद् अरण्यम् अभि यच् चरन्ति
त्वद्भीताः सौम्यताम् आश्रयन्ते
त्वद्भीताः सोमपानं भजन्ते

125.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ bruvatyāṃ tasyāṃ tām āha dakṣiṇadikpatiḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं ब्रुवत्यां तस्यां ताम् आह दक्षिणदिक्पतिः ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
As she was speaking thus, the lord of the southern quarter said to her:

125.s:
yama uvāca
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te dāsye 'haṃ manasaḥ priyam //
125.d:
यम उवाच
वरं वरय भद्रं ते दास्ये ऽहं मनसः प्रियम् ॥
125.m:
Yama said:
Choose a boon, good fortune to you! I will grant what is pleasing to your mind.

125.s:
brahmovāca
yamasyeti vacaḥ śrutvā sā tam āha pativratā //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यमस्येति वचः श्रुत्वा सा तम् आह पतिव्रता ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing this word of Yama, that devoted wife said to him:

125.s:
ulūky uvāca
bhartā me veṣṭitaḥ pāśair daṇḍenābhihatas tava
tasmād rakṣa suraśreṣṭha putrān bhartāram eva ca //
125.d:
उलूक्य् उवाच
भर्ता मे वेष्टितः पाशैर् दण्डेनाभिहतस् तव
तस्माद् रक्ष सुरश्रेष्ठ पुत्रान् भर्तारम् एव च ॥
125.m:
The female owl said:
My husband is bound by the nooses, struck by your staff.
Therefore, best of gods, protect my sons and my husband!

125.s:
brahmovāca
tadvākyāt kṛpayā yukto yamaḥ prāha punaḥ punaḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद्वाक्यात् कृपया युक्तो यमः प्राह पुनः पुनः ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
Moved with compassion by her speech, Yama said again and again:

125.s:
yama uvāca
pāśānāṃ cāpi daṇḍasya sthānaṃ vada śubhānane //
125.d:
यम उवाच
पाशानां चापि दण्डस्य स्थानं वद शुभानने ॥
125.m:
Yama said:
Tell me the place for the nooses and the staff, fair-faced one!

125.s:
brahmovāca
sā provāca yamaṃ devaṃ mayi pāśās tvayeritāḥ
āviśantu jagannātha daṇḍo mayy eva saṃviśet
tataḥ provāca bhagavān yamas tāṃ kṛpayā punaḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सा प्रोवाच यमं देवं मयि पाशास् त्वयेरिताः
आविशन्तु जगन्नाथ दण्डो मय्य् एव संविशेत्
ततः प्रोवाच भगवान् यमस् तां कृपया पुनः ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
She said to god Yama: “Let the nooses dispatched by you
enter into me, Lord of the Universe, and let the staff enter only into me.”
Then the blessed Yama, out of compassion, spoke to her again:

125.s:
yama uvāca
tava bhartā ca putrāś ca sarve jīvantu vijvarāḥ //
125.d:
यम उवाच
तव भर्ता च पुत्राश् च सर्वे जीवन्तु विज्वराः ॥
125.m:
Yama said:
May your husband and all your sons live free from suffering!

125.s:
brahmovāca
nyavārayad yamaḥ pāśān āgneyāstraṃ tu havyavāṭ
kapotolūkayoś cāpi prītiṃ vai cakratuḥ surau
āhatuś ca dvijanmānau vriyatāṃ vara īpsitaḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
न्यवारयद् यमः पाशान् आग्नेयास्त्रं तु हव्यवाट्
कपोतोलूकयोश् चापि प्रीतिं वै चक्रतुः सुरौ
आहतुश् च द्विजन्मानौ व्रियतां वर ईप्सितः ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
Yama checked the nooses, and the bearer of oblations [checked] the weapon of Agni.
The two gods showed affection to the dove and the owl,
and said: “O twice-born ones, let a desired boon be chosen!”

125.s:
pakṣiṇāv ūcatuḥ
bhavator darśanaṃ labdhaṃ vairavyājena duṣkaram
vayaṃ ca pakṣiṇaḥ pāpāḥ kiṃ vareṇa surottamau //
125.d:
पक्षिणाव् ऊचतुः
भवतोर् दर्शनं लब्धं वैरव्याजेन दुष्करम्
वयं च पक्षिणः पापाः किं वरेण सुरोत्तमौ ॥
125.m:
The two birds said:
Sight of you two, difficult to attain, was obtained on the pretext of enmity.
And we are sinful birds; what need is there of a boon, best of gods?

125.s:
atha deyo varo 'smākaṃ bhavadbhyāṃ prītipūrvakam
nātmārtham anuyācāvo dīyamānaṃ varaṃ śubham //
125.d:
अथ देयो वरो ऽस्माकं भवद्भ्यां प्रीतिपूर्वकम्
नात्मार्थम् अनुयाचावो दीयमानं वरं शुभम् ॥
125.m:
If a boon is to be given to us by you two out of affection,
we do not ask for the auspicious boon being granted for our own sake.

125.s:
ātmārthaṃ yas tu yāceta sa śocyo hi sureśvarau
jīvitaṃ saphalaṃ tasya yaḥ parārthodyataḥ sadā //
125.d:
आत्मार्थं यस् तु याचेत स शोच्यो हि सुरेश्वरौ
जीवितं सफलं तस्य यः परार्थोद्यतः सदा ॥
125.m:
He who asks for his own sake is pitiable, lords of gods.
Fruitful is the life of him who is always intent upon the sake of others.

125.s:
agnir āpo raviḥ pṛthvī dhānyāni vividhāni ca
parārthaṃ vartanaṃ teṣāṃ satāṃ cāpi viśeṣataḥ //
125.d:
अग्निर् आपो रविः पृथ्वी धान्यानि विविधानि च
परार्थं वर्तनं तेषां सतां चापि विशेषतः ॥
125.m:
Fire, water, the sun, the earth, and the various grains—
their existence is for the sake of others, and especially that of good people.

125.s:
brahmādayo 'pi hi yato yujyante mṛtyunā saha
evaṃ jñātvā tu deveśau vṛthā svārthapariśramaḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्मादयो ऽपि हि यतो युज्यन्ते मृत्युना सह
एवं ज्ञात्वा तु देवेशौ वृथा स्वार्थपरिश्रमः ॥
125.m:
Since even Brahmā and the others are united with death,
knowing this, lords of gods, exertion for one's own sake is futile.

125.s:
janmanā saha yat puṃsāṃ vihitaṃ parameṣṭhinā
kadācin nānyathā tad vai vṛthā kliśyanti jantavaḥ //
125.d:
जन्मना सह यत् पुंसां विहितं परमेष्ठिना
कदाचिन् नान्यथा तद् वै वृथा क्लिश्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥
125.m:
What is ordained by the Supreme Lord along with a person's birth
can never be otherwise; living beings suffer in vain.

125.s:
tasmād yācāvahe kiṃcid dhitāya jagatāṃ śubham
guṇadāyi tu sarveṣāṃ tad yuvām anumanyatām //
125.d:
तस्माद् याचावहे किंचिद् धिताय जगतां शुभम्
गुणदायि तु सर्वेषां तद् युवाम् अनुमन्यताम् ॥
125.m:
Therefore we ask for something auspicious for the welfare of the worlds,
which bestows virtues upon all; may you two assent to that!

125.s:
brahmovāca
tāv āhatur ubhau devau pakṣiṇau lokaviśrutau
dharmasya yaśaso 'vāptye lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ताव् आहतुर् उभौ देवौ पक्षिणौ लोकविश्रुतौ
धर्मस्य यशसो ऽवाप्त्ये लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥

125.s:
pakṣiṇāv ūcatuḥ
āvābhyām āśramau tīrthe gaṅgāyā ubhaye taṭe
bhavetāṃ jagatāṃ nāthāv eṣa eva paro varaḥ //
125.d:
पक्षिणाव् ऊचतुः
आवाभ्याम् आश्रमौ तीर्थे गङ्गाया उभये तटे
भवेतां जगतां नाथाव् एष एव परो वरः ॥
125.m:
The two birds said:
May there be hermitages for us two at the holy bath on both banks of the Gaṅgā,
O lords of the worlds; this alone is the supreme boon!

125.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṝṇāṃ cāpi pūjanam
sukṛtī duṣkṛtī vāpi yaḥ karoti yathā tathā
sarvaṃ tad akṣayaṃ puṇyaṃ syād ity eṣa paro varaḥ //
125.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः पितॄणां चापि पूजनम्
सुकृती दुष्कृती वापि यः करोति यथा तथा
सर्वं तद् अक्षयं पुण्यं स्याद् इत्य् एष परो वरः ॥
125.m:
Bathing, giving, recitation, oblation, and worship of the ancestors—
whoever performs them, whether an evildoer or a virtuous person, in whatever manner,
may all that become inexhaustible merit: this is the supreme boon.

125.s:
devāv ūcatuḥ
evam astu tathā cānyat suprītau tu bravāvahai //
125.d:
देवाव् ऊचतुः
एवम् अस्तु तथा चान्यत् सुप्रीतौ तु ब्रवावहै ॥
125.m:
The two gods said:
So be it! And another [boon], being well-pleased, we two shall declare.

125.s:
yama uvāca
uttare gautamītīre yamastotraṃ paṭhanti ye
teṣāṃ saptasu vaṃśeṣu nākāle mṛtyum āpnuyāt //
125.d:
यम उवाच
उत्तरे गौतमीतीरे यमस्तोत्रं पठन्ति ये
तेषां सप्तसु वंशेषु नाकाले मृत्युम् आप्नुयात् ॥
125.m:
Yama said:
Those who recite the hymn to Yama on the northern bank of the Gautamī—
among their seven lineages no one shall meet an untimely death.

125.s:
puruṣo bhājanaṃ ca syāt sarvadā sarvasaṃpadām
yas tv idaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ mṛtyustotraṃ jitātmavān //
125.d:
पुरुषो भाजनं च स्यात् सर्वदा सर्वसंपदाम्
यस् त्व् इदं पठते नित्यं मृत्युस्तोत्रं जितात्मवान् ॥
125.m:
A person shall always become a vessel of all kinds of prosperity.
And whoever, self-controlled, constantly recites this hymn of death,

125.s:
aṣṭāśītisahasraiś ca vyādhibhir na sa bādhyate
asmiṃs tīrthe dvijaśreṣṭhau trimāsād gurviṇī satī //
125.d:
अष्टाशीतिसहस्रैश् च व्याधिभिर् न स बाध्यते
अस्मिंस् तीर्थे द्विजश्रेष्ठौ त्रिमासाद् गुर्विणी सती ॥
125.m:
is not afflicted by eighty-eight thousand diseases.
At this holy bath, best of twice-borns, if a virtuous woman pregnant for three months,

125.s:
arvāgvandhyā ca ṣaṇmāsāt saptāhaṃ snānam ācaret
vīrasūḥ sā bhaven nārī śatāyuḥ sa suto bhavet //
125.d:
अर्वाग्वन्ध्या च षण्मासात् सप्ताहं स्नानम् आचरेत्
वीरसूः सा भवेन् नारी शतायुः स सुतो भवेत् ॥
125.m:
or a barren woman within six months, should bathe for seven days,
that woman will become the mother of a hero, and that son will live a hundred years,

125.s:
lakṣmīvān matimāñ śūraḥ putrapautravivardhanaḥ
tatra piṇḍādidānena pitaro muktim āpnuyuḥ
manovākkāyajāt pāpāt snānān mukto bhaven naraḥ //
125.d:
लक्ष्मीवान् मतिमाञ् शूरः पुत्रपौत्रविवर्धनः
तत्र पिण्डादिदानेन पितरो मुक्तिम् आप्नुयुः
मनोवाक्कायजात् पापात् स्नानान् मुक्तो भवेन् नरः ॥

125.s:
brahmovāca
yamavākyād anu tathā havyavāḍ āha pakṣiṇau //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यमवाक्याद् अनु तथा हव्यवाड् आह पक्षिणौ ॥
125.m:
Brahmā said:
After the word of Yama, the bearer of oblations likewise said to the two birds:

125.s:
agnir uvāca
matstotraṃ dakṣiṇe tīre ye paṭhanti yatavratāḥ
teṣām ārogyam aiśvaryaṃ lakṣmīṃ rūpaṃ dadāmy aham //
125.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
मत्स्तोत्रं दक्षिणे तीरे ये पठन्ति यतव्रताः
तेषाम् आरोग्यम् ऐश्वर्यं लक्ष्मीं रूपं ददाम्य् अहम् ॥
125.m:
Agni said:
Those of controlled vows who recite my hymn on the southern bank,
to them I give health, sovereignty, fortune, and beauty.

125.s:
idaṃ stotraṃ tu yaḥ kaścid yatra kvāpi paṭhen naraḥ
naivāgnito bhayaṃ tasya likhite 'pi gṛhe sthite //
125.d:
इदं स्तोत्रं तु यः कश्चिद् यत्र क्वापि पठेन् नरः
नैवाग्नितो भयं तस्य लिखिते ऽपि गृहे स्थिते ॥
125.m:
Whatever person recites this hymn anywhere at all,
he has no fear from fire, even when it is written and remains in the house.

125.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ ca yaḥ kuryād agnitīrthe śucir naraḥ
agniṣṭomaphalaṃ tasya bhaved eva na saṃśayaḥ //
125.d:
स्नानं दानं च यः कुर्याद् अग्नितीर्थे शुचिर् नरः
अग्निष्टोमफलं तस्य भवेद् एव न संशयः ॥
125.m: The pure person who bathes and gives gifts at Agnitīrtha / attains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice; of this there is no doubt.

125.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ yāmyam āgneyam eva ca
kapotaṃ ca tatholūkaṃ hetyulūkaṃ vidur budhāḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं याम्यम् आग्नेयम् एव च
कपोतं च तथोलूकं हेत्युलूकं विदुर् बुधाः ॥
125.m: Brahmā said: / From then on, the wise know that tīrtha as Yāmya, Āgneya, / Kapota, Ulūka, and Hetyulūka.

125.s:
tatra trīṇi sahasrāṇi tāvanty eva śatāni ca
punar navatitīrthāni pratyekaṃ muktibhājanam //
125.d:
तत्र त्रीणि सहस्राणि तावन्त्य् एव शतानि च
पुनर् नवतितीर्थानि प्रत्येकं मुक्तिभाजनम् ॥
125.m: There are three thousand and three hundred, / and also ninety tīrthas there, each an abode of liberation.

125.s:
teṣu snānena dānena pretībhūtāś ca ye narāḥ
pūtās te putravittāḍhyā ākrameyur divaṃ śubhāḥ //
125.d:
तेषु स्नानेन दानेन प्रेतीभूताश् च ये नराः
पूतास् ते पुत्रवित्ताढ्या आक्रमेयुर् दिवं शुभाः ॥
125.m: Through bathing and giving gifts in them, even men who have become spirits / become purified, rich in sons and wealth, and, auspicious, ascend to heaven.

126.s:
brahmovāca
tapastīrtham iti khyātaṃ tapovṛddhikaraṃ mahat
sarvakāmapradaṃ puṇyaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītivardhanam //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तपस्तीर्थम् इति ख्यातं तपोवृद्धिकरं महत्
सर्वकामप्रदं पुण्यं पितॄणां प्रीतिवर्धनम् ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / Celebrated as Tapastīrtha, it brings great increase of ascetic heat; / it grants all desires, is holy, and increases the delight of the ancestors.

126.s:
tasmiṃs tīrthe tu yad vṛttaṃ śṛṇu pāpapraṇāśanam
apām agneś ca saṃvādam ṛṣīṇāṃ ca parasparam //
126.d:
तस्मिंस् तीर्थे तु यद् वृत्तं शृणु पापप्रणाशनम्
अपाम् अग्नेश् च संवादम् ऋषीणां च परस्परम् ॥
126.m: Listen to what happened at that tīrtha, which destroys sins: / the dialogue between the waters and fire, and the sages with one another.

126.s:
apo jyeṣṭhatamāḥ kecin menire 'gniṃ tathāpare
evaṃ bruvanto munayaḥ saṃvādaṃ cāgnivāriṇoḥ //
126.d:
अपो ज्येष्ठतमाः केचिन् मेनिरे ऽग्निं तथापरे
एवं ब्रुवन्तो मुनयः संवादं चाग्निवारिणोः ॥
126.m: Some considered the waters to be the eldest, and others likewise fire. / As the sages were speaking thus, [there arose] the dialogue between fire and water.

126.s:
vināgniṃ jīvanaṃ kva syāj jīvabhūto yato 'nalaḥ
ātmabhūto havyabhūtaś cāgninā jāyate 'khilam //
126.d:
विनाग्निं जीवनं क्व स्याज् जीवभूतो यतो ऽनलः
आत्मभूतो हव्यभूतश् चाग्निना जायते ऽखिलम् ॥
126.m: [The fire-advocates argued:] Without fire, where would life be, since fire has become the vital soul? / Having become the self, having become the oblation, everything is born through fire.

126.s:
agninā dhriyate loko hy agnir jyotirmayaṃ jagat
tasmād agneḥ paraṃ nāsti pāvanaṃ daivataṃ mahat //
126.d:
अग्निना ध्रियते लोको ह्य् अग्निर् ज्योतिर्मयं जगत्
तस्माद् अग्नेः परं नास्ति पावनं दैवतं महत् ॥
126.m: By fire the world is sustained, for the world is composed of fire's light; / therefore, higher than fire there is no purifier, no great deity.

126.s:
antarjyotiḥ sa evoktaḥ paraṃ jyotiḥ sa eva hi
vināgninā kiṃcid asti yasya dhāma jagattrayam //
126.d:
अन्तर्ज्योतिः स एवोक्तः परं ज्योतिः स एव हि
विनाग्निना किंचिद् अस्ति यस्य धाम जगत्त्रयम् ॥
126.m: He alone is spoken of as the inner light; he indeed is the supreme light. / Is there anything without fire, whose abode is the three worlds?

126.s:
tasmād agneḥ paraṃ nāsti bhūtānāṃ jyaiṣṭhyabhājanam
yoṣitkṣetre 'rpitaṃ bījaṃ puruṣeṇa yathā tathā //
126.d:
तस्माद् अग्नेः परं नास्ति भूतानां ज्यैष्ठ्यभाजनम्
योषित्क्षेत्रे ऽर्पितं बीजं पुरुषेण यथा तथा ॥
126.m: Therefore, higher than fire there is none among beings that possesses primacy. / Just as the seed is deposited by a man into the field of a woman,

126.s:
tasya dehādikā śaktiḥ kṛśānor eva nānyathā
devānāṃ hi mukhaṃ vahnis tasmān nātaḥ paraṃ viduḥ //
126.d:
तस्य देहादिका शक्तिः कृशानोर् एव नान्यथा
देवानां हि मुखं वह्निस् तस्मान् नातः परं विदुः ॥
126.m: so the power of his body and [organs] belongs to fire alone, not otherwise. / Indeed, fire is the mouth of the gods; therefore they know nothing higher than this.

126.s:
apare tu hy apāṃ jyaiṣṭhyaṃ menire vedavādinaḥ
adbhiḥ saṃpatsyate hy annaṃ śucir adbhiḥ prajāyate //
126.d:
अपरे तु ह्य् अपां ज्यैष्ठ्यं मेनिरे वेदवादिनः
अद्भिः संपत्स्यते ह्य् अन्नं शुचिर् अद्भिः प्रजायते ॥
126.m: Others, however, teachers of the Veda, considered the primacy to belong to the waters: / 'Food is produced by water, and one becomes pure by water;

126.s:
adbhir eva dhṛtaṃ sarvam āpo vai mātaraḥ smṛtāḥ
trailokyajīvanaṃ vāri vadantīti purāvidaḥ //
126.d:
अद्भिर् एव धृतं सर्वम् आपो वै मातरः स्मृताः
त्रैलोक्यजीवनं वारि वदन्तीति पुराविदः ॥
126.m: all is sustained by water alone; the waters are remembered as mothers; / water is the life of the three worlds'—so say the knowers of ancient lore.

126.s:
utpannam amṛtaṃ hy adbhyas tābhyaś cauṣadhisaṃbhavaḥ
agnir jyeṣṭha iti prāhur āpo jyeṣṭhatamāḥ pare //
126.d:
उत्पन्नम् अमृतं ह्य् अद्भ्यस् ताभ्यश् चौषधिसंभवः
अग्निर् ज्येष्ठ इति प्राहुर् आपो ज्येष्ठतमाः परे ॥
126.m: Nectar is produced from water, and from it arises vegetation. / [Some] say fire is the eldest; others, that the waters are the eldest.

126.s:
evaṃ mīmāṃsamānās te ṛṣayo vedavādinaḥ
viruddhavādino māṃ ca samabhyetyedam abruvan //
126.d:
एवं मीमांसमानास् ते ऋषयो वेदवादिनः
विरुद्धवादिनो मां च समभ्येत्येदम् अब्रुवन् ॥
126.m: Deliberating thus, those sages, exponents of the Veda, / maintaining contradictory views, came to me and spoke these words:

126.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
agner apāṃ vada jyaiṣṭhyaṃ trailokyasya bhavān prabhuḥ //
126.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
अग्नेर् अपां वद ज्यैष्ठ्यं त्रैलोक्यस्य भवान् प्रभुः ॥
126.m: The sages said: / Declare the primacy of fire or of the waters; you are the lord of the three worlds.

126.s:
brahmovāca
aham apy abravaṃ prāptān ṛṣīn sarvān yatavratān
ubhau pūjyatamau loka ubhābhyāṃ jāyate jagat //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अहम् अप्य् अब्रवं प्राप्तान् ऋषीन् सर्वान् यतव्रतान्
उभौ पूज्यतमौ लोक उभाभ्यां जायते जगत् ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / I too said to the sages who had arrived, all of them strictly keeping vows: / 'Both are most worshipful in the world; through both the universe is born.

126.s:
ubhābhyāṃ jāyate havyaṃ kavyaṃ cāmṛtam eva ca
ubhābhyāṃ jīvanaṃ loke śarīrasya ca dhāraṇam //
126.d:
उभाभ्यां जायते हव्यं कव्यं चामृतम् एव च
उभाभ्यां जीवनं लोके शरीरस्य च धारणम् ॥
126.m: Through both the oblations to gods and ancestors are produced, and also nectar. / Through both there is life in the world and the sustenance of the body.

126.s:
nānayoś ca viśeṣo 'sti tato jyaiṣṭhyaṃ samaṃ matam
tato madvacanāj jyaiṣṭhyam ubhayor naiva kasyacit //
126.d:
नानयोश् च विशेषो ऽस्ति ततो ज्यैष्ठ्यं समं मतम्
ततो मद्वचनाज् ज्यैष्ठ्यम् उभयोर् नैव कस्यचित् ॥
126.m: There is no distinction between them; hence their seniority is considered equal.' / Then, by my word, primacy did not belong to either one.

126.s:
jyaiṣṭhyam anyatarasyeti menire ṛṣisattamāḥ
na tṛptā mama vākyena jagmur vāyuṃ tapasvinaḥ //
126.d:
ज्यैष्ठ्यम् अन्यतरस्येति मेनिरे ऋषिसत्तमाः
न तृप्ता मम वाक्येन जग्मुर् वायुं तपस्विनः ॥
126.m: The best of sages considered that primacy must belong to one or the other; / unsatisfied with my statement, the ascetics went to Vāyu.

126.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kasya jyaiṣṭhyaṃ bhavān prāṇo vāyo satyaṃ tvayi sthitam //
126.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
कस्य ज्यैष्ठ्यं भवान् प्राणो वायो सत्यं त्वयि स्थितम् ॥
126.m: The sages said: / Whose is the primacy? You are the vital breath, O Vāyu; truth abides in you.

126.s:
brahmovāca
vāyur āhānalo jyeṣṭhaḥ sarvam agnau pratiṣṭhitam
nety uktvānyonyam ṛṣayo jagmus te 'pi vasuṃdharām //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वायुर् आहानलो ज्येष्ठः सर्वम् अग्नौ प्रतिष्ठितम्
नेत्य् उक्त्वान्योन्यम् ऋषयो जग्मुस् ते ऽपि वसुंधराम् ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / Vāyu said, 'Fire is the eldest; everything is established in fire.' / Saying 'No' to one another, those sages also went to the earth.

126.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
satyaṃ bhūme vada jyaiṣṭhyam ādhārāsi carācare //
126.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
सत्यं भूमे वद ज्यैष्ठ्यम् आधारासि चराचरे ॥
126.m: The sages said: / O Earth, declare the truth of seniority; you are the support of the moving and unmoving.

126.s:
brahmovāca
bhūmir apy āha vinayād āgatāṃs tān ṛṣīn idam //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भूमिर् अप्य् आह विनयाद् आगतांस् तान् ऋषीन् इदम् ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / The earth, too, out of modesty, spoke thus to those sages who had come:

126.s:
bhūmir uvāca
mamāpy ādhārabhūtāḥ syur āpo devyaḥ sanātanāḥ
adbhyas tu jāyate sarvaṃ jyaiṣṭhyam apsu pratiṣṭhitam //
126.d:
भूमिर् उवाच
ममाप्य् आधारभूताः स्युर् आपो देव्यः सनातनाः
अद्भ्यस् तु जायते सर्वं ज्यैष्ठ्यम् अप्सु प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
126.m: The earth said: / Even of me, the divine, eternal waters are the support. / Everything is born from the waters; primacy is established in the waters.

126.s:
brahmovāca
nety uktvānyonyam ṛṣayo jagmuḥ kṣīrodaśāyinam
tuṣṭuvur vividhaiḥ stotraiḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharam //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नेत्य् उक्त्वान्योन्यम् ऋषयो जग्मुः क्षीरोदशायिनम्
तुष्टुवुर् विविधैः स्तोत्रैः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / Saying 'No' to one another, the sages went to the one who reclines upon the ocean of milk; / they praised with various hymns the holder of the conch, discus, and mace.

126.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
yo veda sarvaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhaviṣyad
yaj jāyamānaṃ ca guhāniviṣṭam
lokatrayaṃ citravicitrarūpam
ante samastaṃ ca yam āviveśa
126.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
यो वेद सर्वं भुवनं भविष्यद्
यज् जायमानं च गुहानिविष्टम्
लोकत्रयं चित्रविचित्ररूपम्
अन्ते समस्तं च यम् आविवेश
126.m: The sages said: / He who knows all the world that is to be, / that which is being born, and that which is entered into the cave [of the heart]; / the three worlds of varied and manifold forms, / and into whom everything has entered at the end—

126.s:
yad akṣaraṃ śāśvatam aprameyaṃ
yaṃ vedavedyam ṛṣayo vadanti
yam āśritāḥ svepsitam āpnuvanti
tad vastu satyaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmaḥ
126.d:
यद् अक्षरं शाश्वतम् अप्रमेयं
यं वेदवेद्यम् ऋषयो वदन्ति
यम् आश्रिताः स्वेप्सितम् आप्नुवन्ति
तद् वस्तु सत्यं शरणं व्रजामः
126.m: that which is imperishable, eternal, immeasurable, / which the sages declare to be known through the Vedas, / taking refuge in whom they attain their desired [goal]— / to that real entity we go for refuge.

126.s:
bhūtaṃ mahābhūtajagatpradhānaṃ
na vindate yogino viṣṇurūpam
tad vaktum ete ṛṣayo 'tra yātāḥ
satyaṃ vadasveha jagannivāsa
126.d:
भूतं महाभूतजगत्प्रधानं
न विन्दते योगिनो विष्णुरूपम्
तद् वक्तुम् एते ऋषयो ऽत्र याताः
सत्यं वदस्वेह जगन्निवास
126.m: The yogins do not comprehend the being, the pradhāna of the gross-elemental universe, / the form of Viṣṇu. / These sages have come here to speak of that; / speak the truth here, O abode of the universe.

126.s:
tvam antarātmākhiladehabhājāṃ
tvam eva sarvaṃ tvayi sarvam īśa
tathāpi jānanti na keapi kutrāpi
aho bhavantaṃ prakṛtiprabhāvāt
126.d:
त्वम् अन्तरात्माखिलदेहभाजां
त्वम् एव सर्वं त्वयि सर्वम् ईश
तथापि जानन्ति न केअपि कुत्रापि
अहो भवन्तं प्रकृतिप्रभावात्
126.m:
You are the inner self of all embodied beings;
you alone are everything, and everything is in you, O Lord!
Yet, through the power of material nature, no one anywhere knows
you, alas, who exist everywhere within and without,
revolving in the form of the universe.

126.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prāha jagaddhātrī daivī vāg aśarīriṇī //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्राह जगद्धात्री दैवी वाग् अशरीरिणी ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / Then the bodiless divine voice, the supporter of the world, spoke:

126.s:
daivī vāg uvāca
ubhāv ārādhya tapasā bhaktyā ca niyamena ca
yasya syāt prathamaṃ siddhis tad bhūtaṃ jyeṣṭham ucyate //
126.d:
दैवी वाग् उवाच
उभाव् आराध्य तपसा भक्त्या च नियमेन च
यस्य स्यात् प्रथमं सिद्धिस् तद् भूतं ज्येष्ठम् उच्यते ॥
126.m: The divine voice said: / Having worshipped both with austerity, devotion, and restraint, / that element to which accomplishment comes first is declared the eldest.

126.s:
brahmovāca
tathety tathā yayuḥ sarve ṛṣayo lokapūjitāḥ
śrāntāḥ khinnāntarātmānaḥ paraṃ vairāgyam āśritāḥ //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् तथा ययुः सर्वे ऋषयो लोकपूजिताः
श्रान्ताः खिन्नान्तरात्मानः परं वैराग्यम् आश्रिताः ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / Saying 'So be it,' all the sages, revered by the world, / weary, grieved in their inner selves, took resort to supreme dispassion.

126.s:
sarvalokaikajananīṃ bhuvanatrayapāvanīm
gautamīm agaman sarve tapas taptuṃ yatavratāḥ //
126.d:
सर्वलोकैकजननीं भुवनत्रयपावनीम्
गौतमीम् अगमन् सर्वे तपस् तप्तुं यतव्रताः ॥
126.m: To the sole mother of all worlds, the purifier of the three realms, / to the Gautamī they all went, keeping their vows, to perform austerity.

126.s:
abdaivataṃ tathāgniṃ ca pūjanāyodyatās tadā
agneś ca pūjakā ye ca apāṃ vai pūjane sthitāḥ
tatra vāg abravīd daivī vedamātā sarasvatī //
126.d:
अब्दैवतं तथाग्निं च पूजनायोद्यतास् तदा
अग्नेश् च पूजका ये च अपां वै पूजने स्थिताः
तत्र वाग् अब्रवीद् दैवी वेदमाता सरस्वती ॥
126.m: Then, eager to worship the water-deity and also fire, / some were worshippers of fire, and some engaged in the worship of the waters. / There the divine voice, Sarasvatī, the mother of the Vedas, spoke:

126.s:
daivī vāg uvāca
agner āpas tathā yonir adbhiḥ śaucam avāpyate
agneś ca pūjakā ye ca vinādbhiḥ pūjanaṃ katham //
126.d:
दैवी वाग् उवाच
अग्नेर् आपस् तथा योनिर् अद्भिः शौचम् अवाप्यते
अग्नेश् च पूजका ये च विनाद्भिः पूजनं कथम् ॥
126.m: The divine voice said: / Water is the source of fire; purity is obtained through water. / And those who are worshippers of fire—how can worship be done without water?

126.s:
apsu jātāsu sarvatra karmaṇy adhikṛto bhavet
tāvat karmaṇy anarho 'yam aśucir malino naraḥ //
126.d:
अप्सु जातासु सर्वत्र कर्मण्य् अधिकृतो भवेत्
तावत् कर्मण्य् अनर्हो ऽयम् अशुचिर् मलिनो नरः ॥
126.m: Only when water is present is one everywhere qualified for religious rites; / until then a man is unfit for rites, impure and stained.

126.s:
na magnaḥ śraddhayā yāvad apsu śītāsu vedavit
tasmād āpo variṣṭhāḥ syur mātṛbhūtā yataḥ smṛtāḥ
tasmāj jyaiṣṭhyam apām eva jananyo 'gner viśeṣataḥ //
126.d:
न मग्नः श्रद्धया यावद् अप्सु शीतासु वेदवित्
तस्माद् आपो वरिष्ठाः स्युर् मातृभूता यतः स्मृताः
तस्माज् ज्यैष्ठ्यम् अपाम् एव जनन्यो ऽग्नेर् विशेषतः ॥
126.m: A knower of the Veda is not [qualified] until he is immersed with faith in cold waters. / Therefore the waters are the highest, since they are remembered as mothers; / therefore primacy belongs to the waters alone, especially as they are the mothers of fire.

126.s:
brahmovāca
etad vacaḥ śuśruvus te ṛṣayo vedavādinaḥ
niścayaṃ ca tataś cakrur bhavej jyaiṣṭhyam apām iti //
126.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतद् वचः शुश्रुवुस् ते ऋषयो वेदवादिनः
निश्चयं च ततश् चक्रुर् भवेज् ज्यैष्ठ्यम् अपाम् इति ॥
126.m: Brahmā said: / Those sages who profess the Veda heard these words; / and then they resolved: 'Water indeed is the foremost.'

126.s:
yatra tīrthe vṛttam idam ṛṣisattre ca nārada
tapastīrthaṃ tu tat proktaṃ sattratīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
126.d:
यत्र तीर्थे वृत्तम् इदम् ऋषिसत्त्रे च नारद
तपस्तीर्थं तु तत् प्रोक्तं सत्त्रतीर्थं तद् उच्यते ॥
126.m: The tīrtha where this happened in that sages' sacrificial session, O Nārada, / is called Tapastīrtha, and it is also known as Sattratīrtha.

126.s:
agnitīrthaṃ ca tat proktaṃ tathā sārasvataṃ viduḥ
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham //
126.d:
अग्नितीर्थं च तत् प्रोक्तं तथा सारस्वतं विदुः
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च सर्वकामप्रदं शुभम् ॥
126.m: It is called Agnitīrtha as well, and the wise know it as Sārasvata. / Bathing and making gifts there is auspicious and grants all desires.

126.s:
caturdaśa śatāny atra tīrthānāṃ puṇyadāyinām
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca svargamokṣapradāyakam //
126.d:
चतुर्दश शतान्य् अत्र तीर्थानां पुण्यदायिनाम्
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदायकम् ॥
126.m: Fourteen hundred merit-bestowing tīrthas are found here. / Bathing and making gifts in them grants heaven and liberation.

126.s:
kṛtaṃ saṃdehaharaṇam ṛṣīṇāṃ yatra bhāṣayā
sarasvaty abhavat tatra gaṅgayā saṃgatā nadī
māhātmyaṃ tasya ko vaktuṃ saṃgamasya kṣamo naraḥ //
126.d:
कृतं संदेहहरणम् ऋषीणां यत्र भाषया
सरस्वत्य् अभवत् तत्र गङ्गया संगता नदी
माहात्म्यं तस्य को वक्तुं संगमस्य क्षमो नरः ॥
126.m: Where the doubt of the sages was resolved by speech, / the river Sarasvatī there became united with the Gaṅgā. / What mortal is capable of describing the greatness of that confluence?

127.s:
brahmovāca
devatīrtham iti khyātaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
127.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
देवतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं गङ्गाया उत्तरे तटे
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
127.m: Brahmā said: / On the northern bank of the Gaṅgā is the famous Devatīrtha; / I shall recount its power, which destroys all sins.

127.s:
ārṣṭiṣeṇa iti khyāto rājā sarvaguṇānvitaḥ
tasya bhāryā jayā nāma sākṣāl lakṣmīr ivāparā //
127.d:
आर्ष्टिषेण इति ख्यातो राजा सर्वगुणान्वितः
तस्य भार्या जया नाम साक्षाल् लक्ष्मीर् इवापरा ॥
127.m: There was a king named Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, endowed with every virtue; / his wife, named Jayā, was like Lakṣmī herself embodied.

127.s:
tasya putro bharo nāma matimān pitṛvatsalaḥ
dhanurvede ca vede ca niṣṇāto dakṣa eva ca //
127.d:
तस्य पुत्रो भरो नाम मतिमान् पितृवत्सलः
धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च निष्णातो दक्ष एव च ॥
127.m: His son, named Bhara, was intelligent and devoted to his father, / fully accomplished in the science of archery and the Veda, and proficient indeed.

127.s:
tasya bhāryā rūpavatī suprabhety abhiviśrutā
ārṣṭiṣeṇas tato rājā putre rājyaṃ niveśya saḥ //
127.d:
तस्य भार्या रूपवती सुप्रभेत्य् अभिविश्रुता
आर्ष्टिषेणस् ततो राजा पुत्रे राज्यं निवेश्य सः ॥
